type: apDisplay, a brand grotesque, is the only family: weight 500, sentence case, slightly tight. Body 16-18px; section headings in dark red reach about 5.9vw. The hero has no typographic headline, the sticker logo plays that role. Labels inside sticker tabs go bold.
colour: #dc1928 #fdf3db #952625 #e0a912 #5b7a94 #d46831 — Post red and cream alternate as full section fields; mustard, slate blue, burnt orange and maroon are reserved for card frames and badges. Warm, flat, no gradients.
imagery: Flat vector drawings (parcel, locker, hand holding a card) with thick cream die-cut outlines and hard offset shadows, plus candid photos of people at lockers placed inside arch-shaped cut-outs and wide rounded video tiles.
layout: Every section is a centre-stacked composition on a full-width colour field, with a pill-shaped sticky sub-nav top-centre after the hero. Sections are separated by ornament rather than whitespace: a red and cream checkerboard strip, a scalloped awning edge. Cards come in tilted rows of three or five.

sections.description: On red beneath a checkerboard strip, a dark-red pill with a dotted inner border holds the heading. Three statistics are scattered as tilted stickers instead of a row: a mustard circle, a maroon starburst seal with a cursor-arrow sticker overlapping it, and a slate-blue tag shape, each with a small parcel or locker illustration tucked onto a corner. Figures are large; captions are tiny and centred inside each shape.

On cream, the heading sits in a white rounded box with dark-red outline and offset shadow, hanging directly under the sticky nav. Below, three equal portrait cards in mustard, slate blue and orange, each with a dark-red border and hard offset shadow, containing an arch-shaped photo cut-out of people, a tilted name-tag sticker, a starburst date badge, two centred lines of copy and a small white pill button.

A centred locker illustration with icon stickers orbiting it, a centred heading and two-line intro, then a full-width two-by-two mosaic of video stills with no gaps and rounded outer corners. Each tile carries one large white rounded chip with a bold red word, placed low and off-centre. A hand-drawn orange arrow sticker overlaps the mosaic's top-left corner, pointing in.

Five stacked white pill-shaped rows in a centred column about 65% of the page wide, each with dark-red outline, hard offset shadow, question at left and chevron at right. A checkerboard strip then returns the page to red, where an oversized version of the sticker logo sits centred with a one-line copyright beneath.

steal: Turn the primary navigation into a fan of tilted illustrated cards in the hero, centre card upright and the outer ones rotated and cropped by the viewport edges.
Give every element the same die-cut sticker treatment (thick cream outline plus a hard, unblurred offset shadow in a darker shade of the background) so buttons, cards and badges read as one family.
Present statistics as differently shaped badges (circle, starburst, tag) scattered at angles rather than as three equal columns.

name: Rows
idea: Radical understatement: a product about simple lists is sold with a 27px headline, 12px copy and a column of small live demos, each proving one interaction.
hero: Warm off-white page, almost empty. Everything hangs on one vertical line 27% in from the left. A small striped-letter logo mark sits there near the top; 220px lower comes a two-line headline at only 27px (under 2vw), then three lines of 13px body about 370px wide, then a near-black rectangular button with 4px corners beside a text link with an arrow. A single grey sign-in link sits in the top-right corner; there is no navigation bar. More than 80% of the viewport is blank. At the bottom edge the first feature module peeks in: grey demo panel left, short text column right.
type: Suisse Intl only, weight 450–500, tracking −0.04em. Headline 27px, feature headings about 16px on two lines, body 12px. Three sizes in total, no uppercase and no display moment; hierarchy comes from weight and empty space alone.
colour: #f5f6f1 #e6e7e1 #1a191d #ffffff #c7372f #3aa56a — Warm paper off-white with slightly darker grey-green demo panels and near-black type; colour appears only inside the UI as priority dots, outlined status pills and one green or red action button.
imagery: No pictures: small live-rendered fragments of the app (two or three white list rows with dots, status pills, avatars and a visible cursor) sit in flat grey panels of fixed 368px width with barely rounded corners.
layout: One content block about 650px wide, offset left of centre, repeated down the page: 368px demo panel plus a 245px text column, top-aligned, separated by 200px or more of empty space. The logo mark sticks to the top-left corner on scroll. Footer is one line.

sections.description: The repeating module: a flat grey panel roughly 368px wide and 120–190px tall holding a tiny mock list (white rows with 6px radius, a coloured numbered dot at left, task title, an outlined status pill, an avatar, a chevron) and often a cursor mid-action. To its right, 20px away and top-aligned, a medium-weight heading of one or two lines and two short paragraphs at 11–12px in a column only 245px wide. Modules never alternate sides; they stack with large gaps.

The closing block keeps the same narrow measure: a three-line paragraph at 13px, then the identical button and arrow-link pair from the hero, left-aligned on the text column's axis. After a long gap a single hairline spans the 650px block and under it sits one row of tiny footer text: brand line at left, six links and a copyright strung along the right.

steal: Set the headline at near-body size (under 2vw) and let empty space, not scale, give it importance.
Explain each feature with a tiny cropped fragment of real UI in a fixed-width flat panel, one interaction per panel, with the cursor left visible.
Hang the whole page on one off-centre left edge and never break it, logo and footer included.

name: Shawn Golden
idea: A personal homepage as a lovingly broken desktop: browser-default Times, 1px table borders and a giant pixel-serif name frame a set of working toys (paint program, clock, joke button, character generator).
hero: The whole site is one viewport divided by 1px black lines with no outer margin. Across the top, the name in a brown pixel serif at 14.4vw is cropped by both side edges in a band 170px tall. Under it: four equal bordered link cells with icons, a one-line text ticker, and a bio row with a round portrait and three lines of uppercase Times. The lower 65% is three columns: a 235px left rail (character drawing, work list, a button), a wide centre (large italic email ticker above a dark green paint canvas, dingbats beneath), and a 235px right rail (flipping word, analogue clock, weather line, navy flower panel).
type: PP Mondwest pixel serif for the name only, at 207px. Everything else is unstyled Times New Roman: 13px for links and lists, uppercase 13px for the bio, italic uppercase at about 44px for the email ticker. Links are default blue with underlines.
colour: #ffffff #023627 #ececec #8a6c50 #1f2638 #1a4be0 — White cells with black hairlines; colour arrives as isolated blocks: brown name, dark green canvas, navy flower panel with a pink bloom, pale yellow paper, browser-default link blue.
imagery: Scratchy hand-drawn characters on yellow paper, a flat vector flower animation, a round caricature avatar and the visitor's own pixel doodles; each sits in its own bordered, square-cornered cell.
layout: No scroll and no margins: a table-like grid of bordered cells fills the viewport, 235px rails either side of a wide centre, with full-width strips stacked above. Every cell holds a different widget; hierarchy comes from the oversized name and the central canvas. Mobile stacks cells full-width.

sections.description: Centre cell on light grey: a dark green rectangle about 745×420px is a pixel paint canvas, centred, with a two-by-four grid of 40px square tool buttons (pencil, eraser, spray, hand, two swatches, zoom, fullscreen, trash) plus save and gallery buttons docked at its left edge. Above it a bordered strip scrolls the email address in 44px italic uppercase, link parts in dotted-underline blue; below it a strip of sixteen evenly spaced dingbat glyphs ends in an arrow.

Left rail. A tall cell shows a randomly generated character drawing on a pale yellow rectangle with an underlined text control beneath to request another. Below a rule, a small uppercase heading and four entries: project name as a blue underlined link, client in black Times on the next line, a tiny double arrow at the right edge. At the bottom, a full-width outlined button with centred text.

Right rail stacks four cells: a word that flips vertically between short apologies in 22px Times; a hairline analogue clock about 230px across with the city and digital time printed inside the face; a one-line temperature reading; and a tall navy cell where a pink illustrated flower sways, its stem cropped by the bottom edge.

steal: Divide the viewport into bordered cells with 1px black lines and zero margin, and give each cell one live widget instead of a content section.
Contrast one enormous bitmap-style display word against otherwise completely unstyled default serif text.
Put a small working toy (a paint canvas, a random character generator) at the centre of a personal site so visitors make something before they read anything.

name: Medium Rare
idea: A project index as a messy pile of coloured index cards, each slightly rotated and overlapping the last, stacked under a wordmark that fills the column.
hero: Warm off-white paper-textured page; all content sits in a 920px centred column. A tiny header row: a struck-through-then-corrected tagline left, a small magenta diamond logo centre, a magenta email and a slider-like toggle right. Directly below, the name in black ultra-condensed heavy caps spans the full column width, about 190px tall, its baseline cut by the first card. Four full-column cards follow, each roughly 160px tall with 12px radius and a soft shadow, rotated between -1.5 and +1.5 degrees and overlapping the one above: periwinkle, lime, amber, white. Each carries a 64px condensed title top-left and a faint mono number top-right.
type: Oswald medium at 64px, mixed case, tracking -0.037em, for card titles; a heavier compressed grotesque for the wordmark (probably an image); Inter 14px for the small caps header and card subtitles; a mono for three-digit card numbers. Extreme jump from 190px wordmark to 12px labels.
colour: #f7f7f5 #000000 #97aaf6 #bbf697 #fed878 #6ef8fb — Neutral paper ground and black type; each card gets its own flat pastel or highlighter colour (periwinkle, lime, amber, cyan, yellow, lilac). Hot magenta is reserved for the logo, email and links.
imagery: No images in the list; coloured cards with type are the imagery. A subtle paper grain covers the background and the cards cast soft shadows like physical objects.
layout: One 920px column centred on the page, content left-aligned inside it. Wordmark, then about fifteen overlapping cards in one continuous stack with no section breaks, then a wide gap and a sparse three-column footer. Rhythm comes only from card colour and alternating tilt.

sections.description: Fifteen full-column cards, each around 160px tall with 12px radius, a 1px darker edge and soft shadow, alternating slight clockwise and anticlockwise rotation so edges never align, each overlapping the previous by about 20px like papers dropped on a desk. Title in 64px condensed type top-left with 28px padding, a descending three-digit number in faint mono top-right, and on mobile a one-line grey description under the title. Adjacent colours never repeat.

After about 200px of empty paper, a single row: the wordmark at 30px tall on the left, a small-caps question in the middle, and a grey input with an outlined button on the right. A faint dotted rule follows, then three tiny question-and-answer columns in 10px text with magenta names, and a last line with copyright left and a live clock right.

steal: Rotate each list row by a degree or two in alternating directions and overlap it onto the previous one, turning a plain link list into a pile of cards.
Let the first card overlap and cut the baseline of the giant wordmark so heading and list read as one object.
Number items in descending order with faint mono digits in the corner so the newest sits on top of the stack.

name: Berd
idea: The page types its own headlines into an empty app window, then hands over to toy-like 3D characters and ends on a giant red face delivering a joke testimonial.
archetype: other: typed statement in empty window frame
hero: A warm light-grey field covered by a faint dot grid, with no navigation at first. Centred, a single rounded rectangle 1000px wide and 710px tall (70% of the width, 79% of the height) in a lighter grey, with three tiny traffic-light dots in its top-left corner: an empty application window. In its exact centre a headline at about 42px is typed one character at a time; the capture shows only its first letter. Nothing else is on screen. On scroll the window gives way to 90px words typing onto the bare grid with a cursor line, and a small logo and a black download tag pin to the top corners.
type: Cash Sans at regular weight with -0.04em tracking for everything from 13px body to 90px typed statements; Cash Sans Mono in tiny uppercase for card headers and labels. Body copy is unusually small, so type is either huge or tiny.
colour: #e4e4e0 #f4f4f4 #000000 #c23e29 #fff200 — Grey on grey with black type for most of the page; colour arrives late and at full strength: glossy toy characters, then a red full-bleed close with yellow type and a yellow cursor disc.
imagery: Glossy 3D toy characters (jelly, cube, rock) as cut-outs on cards; looping demo videos inside black tiles with chamfered corners; a macro close-up of a red character's face filling the last screens.
layout: Each screen holds one thing: a window, a typed phrase, a horizontal row of square demo tiles bleeding off both edges, a fanned stack of cards with a small text block at left, a full-bleed face. Large empty grey intervals sit between them.

sections.description: A small centred title, then a single row of roughly 390px-square black tiles running off both sides of the page. Each tile has its four corners cut at 45 degrees, making an octagon, and holds a small inset demo video on black. Under each tile sit a centred one-line caption and a two-line grey quotation of the prompt at about 11px. The row scrolls sideways.

Left third: a tiny monospaced uppercase label, a two-line 24px heading and five lines of small grey text, vertically centred. Right: three portrait cards overlapping like a hand of trading cards, the middle one larger and in front. Each card is off-white with a mono header and serial number, a 3D character cut-out in the upper half, a name at 28px, a short description and two small columns divided by vertical rules.

The grey page ends and a macro video of a shiny red character's face fills the full width for more than a screen of height, eyes at the top and smile at the bottom. Across the nose a two-line quotation in bright yellow at about 90px types itself out, centred. A yellow disc with tiny text follows the pointer. Footer links run in small type along the bottom edge of the footage.

steal: Open on an empty application window and type the headline into it, so the first screen demonstrates the product's premise instead of describing it.
Cut the corners of square media tiles at 45 degrees to give a plain video row its own silhouette.
Save all saturated colour for the final screen: a full-bleed close-up with one oversized quotation set over it.

name: davesocozy
idea: A collage artist introduces himself by building a collage: each scroll step changes one caption and drops more paper cut-outs onto a green cutting mat.
hero: Cream page with a single centred object: a green cutting mat 776px wide by 582px tall (54% of viewport width), printed with a white grid, an inner border and diagonal guide lines, casting a soft shadow. One small portrait photo lies at its exact centre, tilted about three degrees. A one-line greeting in bold monospace at 32px sits 30px above the mat. The four viewport corners hold fixed controls: a glossy green flower logo top-left and three dark brown bevelled buttons in uppercase mono (shop top-right, Instagram bottom-left, enter studio bottom-right). A small scroll cue sits under the mat.
type: Martian Mono everywhere. Bold 32px for the changing caption (one or two centred lines); 12px tracked uppercase for buttons and hints. Only two sizes, and the mono face gives a label-maker feel that suits a workbench.
colour: #ede6d4 #5c894e #241a15 #3d2b22 #ffffff — Warm cream ground, mat green as the one large colour block, chocolate brown for text and buttons. Other colour arrives only through the collage scraps.
imagery: Cut-out vintage imagery (twin-lens camera, game console, microphone, globe, fox, fish, crumpled paper) and one portrait photo, each rotated a few degrees with a slight shadow, scattered on the mat like paper scraps. A 3D room follows.
layout: A single fixed stage: nothing scrolls away, the mat stays centred while its contents and the caption above change. Corner-pinned buttons replace a nav bar. Empty cream margins of about 23% of the width on each side.

sections.description: Scroll-driven introduction on the pinned stage. The caption above the mat is replaced sentence by sentence, each as two centred lines of bold mono, and with every sentence two or three more cut-outs land on the mat around the portrait at loose angles, some overlapping it and a few flying in from outside. By the last caption the mat holds about ten scraps and a line of tiny uppercase instructions appears beneath the caption.

After the intro the mat hands over to a canvas-rendered studio room that the visitor looks around with the mouse and clicks into (the page's own text lists a desk of collages, a wall of framed pieces and a television). The four corner buttons persist as the only chrome. The room itself is not in the captured frames, so its composition is unknown.

steal: Pin one physical work surface in the centre and let scrolling add objects to it while a single caption line above changes, instead of stacking sections.
Put navigation in the four viewport corners as small tactile buttons so the centre stays free.
Rotate every cut-out by a different few degrees and give each a small shadow so flat images read as paper.

name: Nodeck
idea: A consultancy that claims to sell thinking rather than slides builds its site as a slide deck anyway, complete with prev/next buttons, a slide counter and presenter notes.
hero: Flat bubblegum-pink viewport. Centre: the name as a sticker, white ultra-heavy caps with a thick black outline and offset black extrusion, bent along a gentle arc and slightly rotated, about 72% wide and 30% tall. A two-word caps label sits 80px above it; a two-line caps tagline at ~1.1vw sits below, two of its words swiped in fluorescent yellow. Photographic props crop off the corners: a yellow sticky note top-left and a highlighter pen entering top-right whose tip touches the last letter. Bottom edge is deck chrome: notes link left; previous, round lime menu and next buttons with hard black offset shadows centred; mute icon and slide counter right.
type: The wordmark is an SVG sticker in ultra-black caps. Slide titles use BN Dime Display, a fat irregular display sans, uppercase at ~7vw. Everything else is DM Sans uppercase at 14 to 16px regular. Two sizes, a sevenfold jump.
colour: #ff87ab #f5e4d6 #000000 #ffffff #def915 #e9d68b — Each slide is a flat field, pink then cream, with black type; fluorescent lime-yellow is the action and highlight colour (menu button, highlighter swipes, transition wipes). Warm and saturated.
imagery: Top-down cut-out photos of desk stationery (sticky note, highlighter, pink eraser) with soft shadows, cropped by the viewport corners and positioned to touch the type. Otherwise type only.
layout: One fixed full-viewport stage per slide rather than a scrolling page: a centred title or statement in the middle, a small logo sticker pinned top-centre after slide one, and a persistent control bar along the bottom edge. Ten slides.

sections.description: Every slide opens on a cream full-viewport title card carrying only a tiny caps slide-number label and, about 20px beneath it, the slide's title in fat black display caps at ~7vw, centred slightly above the middle. The title rises from behind a mask, then gives way to the slide body on the same stage. A fluorescent yellow brush-stroke band wipes across the screen between slides.

A pink stage with the small sticker logo pinned top-centre and a pink eraser photograph cropped near the top-right corner. A tiny caps slide label sits at one third height; body copy then builds in word by word in heavy caps starting from the left margin at mid-height. The deck controls stay fixed along the bottom edge throughout, with the counter advancing.

steal: Borrow another medium's chrome (deck controls, slide counter, presenter notes) as the site's navigation to make the brand's argument.
Crop real desk objects off the viewport corners and let one physically touch the wordmark so photo and type share a scene.
Use a highlighter swipe both as text emphasis and as the full-screen transition wipe, tying a small detail to the large motion.

name: Vestris
idea: Dry title-settlement software wrapped in a calm painted countryside: gouache-style foliage and skies frame the product so paperwork feels pastoral.
hero: Cream field. Nav in a ~1150px container: serif-italic wordmark with a compass icon left, three links centred, sign-in and an olive rounded button right. A centred stack begins at 17% height: a small bordered backer badge, then a one-line serif headline at ~6.7vw, its last two words italic, flanked by oversized parentheses pushed about 100px away from the words so the line spans 60% of the width. A three-line grey sans paragraph (~570px) and an olive button follow. From 62% height a sky-painted panel rises, holding a browser-framed app screenshot ~900px wide, cropped by the fold. Painted leafy branches grow in from both viewport edges, overlapping cream and panel.
type: Instrument Serif regular at 96px (-0.03em) for headlines, typically one roman line and one italic line; Geist 18px grey for body and 14px for interface text. Section heads sit near 56px. About four sizes; headings are always centred.
colour: #f2efe5 #62654e #bcd3e6 #3f5a2a #fafaf8 #2a2a26 — Warm cream ground, olive buttons, charcoal serif type; sky blue and leaf green arrive only through the painted illustrations. Sections stay cream apart from illustrated panels and the landscape footer.
imagery: Painterly gouache-style illustrations (foliage, clouds, a bee, a handshake framed as a perforated postage stamp, a farmhouse landscape) combined with clean app screenshots in rounded browser frames sitting on the painted skies.
layout: Centred throughout in a ~1150px container: headline, short paragraph, button, then media. Bare cream screens alternate with large rounded sky-painted panels inset about 20px from the viewport edges; three-column card rows hang off the panels. Vertical gaps exceed 150px.

sections.description: A rounded-corner panel inset about 20px from the viewport sides, filled with a soft painted sky and a leaf branch entering bottom-left. Centred inside: a two-line serif heading at ~4vw (roman line, then italic line) and a two-line grey sentence. Three white rounded cards in a row overlap the lower part of the panel, each with a bold sans title and three lines of small copy.

A bare cream screen with a small painted bee inside a faint circle, centred above a two-line serif heading whose first line is roman and second italic. The letters fill from pale grey to charcoal as the reader scrolls (caught mid-word in the capture). A two-line grey sentence sits beneath. Nothing else occupies the viewport.

Three columns. The outer two each hold a centred two-line serif subhead near 28px, four lines of grey copy and a proof line with a small tick icon. The middle column holds a handshake painting cropped as a postage stamp with a perforated white edge, tilted about ten degrees, breaking the row's symmetry of text.

A full-bleed painted landscape (hills, a white farmhouse, a fenced path) about one viewport tall, with a dark green scrim rising from the bottom. Two buttons float over the sky at top centre. The wordmark and a one-line descriptor sit bottom-left, two short link columns bottom-right, and a legal row runs along the base, all in cream.

steal: Widen a short headline by setting it between oversized parentheses spaced far from the words.
Commission one painted illustration style and use it for section backgrounds, spot icons and the footer, with clean interface screenshots sitting on top.
Crop a spot illustration as a perforated postage stamp and tilt it between two text columns to break a three-column row.

name: RSquad
idea: The six letters of the name are detached red monospace glyphs that float over the whole page and reshuffle their constellation as you scroll, while the actual content sits quietly underneath in tiny mono.
hero: White viewport with no imagery. Three tiny uppercase mono nav words sit on the top edge at far left, exact centre and far right, the active one underlined. The wordmark is exploded into six red monospace capitals, each about 12% of viewport height, placed on a loose ring roughly 45% of the viewport wide: R alone at top centre, S and D at mid-left and mid-right, Q and A lower, U at bottom centre, with three small red vertical blocks as punctuation between them. Inside the ring sits a two-line 20px mono tagline, a small hooked arrow and one underlined text link. The outer thirds are empty.
type: Elma Mono Variable at weight 300, uppercase, 20px for nav, taglines and body; the red letters are the same mono enlarged about six times. Cortese Trial, a light flared serif in tight capitals, sets pull quotes at about 4.4vw; Inter for small link captions. Three sizes in total.
colour: #ffffff #fa2420 #111111 #000000 #d9d9d9 — White ground with thin black text and one saturated signal red reserved for the floating letters and blocks; the closing screen inverts to black with white and red line ornaments.
imagery: No photographs. The red letters are the imagery, plus small engraved-style ornamental roman numerals inside dotted selection boxes and, on the last black screen, white line-drawn vines with red star flowers.
layout: One centred column about a third of the viewport wide with huge side margins. Sections are short centred stacks: ornamental numeral, two-word title, mono paragraph, then two or three columns of underlined links with one-line captions. Wide serif quotes break the narrow rhythm.

sections.description: Chapter block: at top centre a tall dotted-outline box with tiny square corner handles, like a selected frame in a design tool, holds an engraved roman numeral and a two-word stacked title; dotted diagonals fan out beneath it like a tent. Below comes a centred two-line mono paragraph, then a row of two or three underlined project names, each marked by a small black square above and a one-line sans caption below.

Pull quote in light serif capitals at roughly 4.4vw, centred, five tightly leaded lines about 60% of viewport width, wrapped in guillemets and filling the top half of the screen. Red mono letters and blocks pass over and between the words, deliberately colliding with the text. No attribution, rule or card; the next numbered chapter box starts directly below.

A three-line mono paragraph centred at the top, then three short sans statements arranged as a triangle (two side by side, one below centre), each topped by a small black square. The block ends with a two-line serif-capitals sign-off at about 4vw, centred, with the red letters clustered directly on top of it.

Closing screen flips to solid black: a second serif-capitals quote in white, centred, with one small mono line above it. White line-drawn vines and red star flowers creep in from the lower corners and right edge, and the red letters now run in a loose vertical chain through the quote. The three-word nav stays pinned in white.

steal: Break the wordmark into single glyphs and place them as a loose ring around the tagline, keeping the centre for a two-line statement and one text link.
Use one typeface at only two extremes (20px mono for everything, the same mono at six times the size in the accent colour) and bring in a serif-capitals face solely for quotes.
Mark chapters with a dotted selection box with corner handles around an ornamental numeral instead of a heading bar or eyebrow.

name: Nia Creative
idea: The three-letter wordmark becomes a slot-machine reel: the name repeats vertically and its middle letter is swapped for a square of client photography or video.
hero: Pale grey field with a slim nav: bracketed lowercase logo top-left, four uppercase mono links centred, a black pill button top-right. The centre 43% of the width holds a vertical reel of the wordmark stacked three times in very heavy black grotesk, each row about 230px tall; in every row the middle letter is replaced by a square photo or video tile (surfers, a woman holding glasses over her eyes, a burger). The middle row is sharp; rows above and below fade out through gradient masks. A bottom strip carries a mono descriptor at left and city plus live clock at right. A plum band starts at the fold.
type: A heavy, tightly tracked grotesk (xgnl) carries the wordmark, a 70px lowercase section word and bold 20 to 34px statements; body is the same face at 14px, bold. Geist Mono in small capitals handles nav, categories, bracketed indexes and the clock.
colour: #f3f3f3 #574d56 #515144 #1c1c1c #b9aebd #b3b586 — Pale grey base with black type. Two muted full-width bands, dusty plum and olive, set their text in a lighter tint of the band colour rather than white. Photography supplies the saturation.
imagery: Flash-lit hospitality and lifestyle photography plus short video: cocktails, hotel rooms, food, trail runners. Portrait tiles with one or two large rounded corners, square tiles inside the wordmark, and an edge-to-edge three-up strip.
layout: 28px side margins and a three-column grid for work. Big lowercase section words sit flush left with a small paragraph flush right. Sections alternate pale grey grids, coloured statement bands and full-bleed image strips; a black rounded nav bar pins to the top after the hero.

sections.description: Dusty plum band about one viewport tall. A bold 34px statement in pale lilac sits top-left across half the width, one phrase underlined with a hand-drawn stroke. Lower left, a small heading and eight industries in tiny uppercase mono split into two bulleted columns. At the right margin a tall portrait photo, about 20% of the width, with large rounded corners, overlaps the band's top edge and leaves the middle of the band empty.

A 70px heavy lowercase word flush left with a three-line 14px paragraph flush right on the same baseline. Below, three equal columns with wide gutters: each has a portrait image narrower than its column with a large radius on the bottom-right corner only, then a 20px project name, a mono uppercase category and a four-line bold description. Rows repeat with no dividers or card backgrounds.

Three photographs or clips butt together edge to edge with no gaps, each a third of the viewport wide and about 40% of a screen tall. Immediately below, an olive band: a three-line 26px statement in pale olive at left with one underlined phrase, two lines of small copy beneath it, and a small rounded portrait image tucked into the lower right corner.

Services as stacked sheets. Each is a full-width panel with a 1px outline and large top-corner radius that slides up over the previous one. The left half is empty except for a centred column: a bracketed mono index, a 26px bold title and four centred lines of sub-services. The right half is one photograph with rounded corners filling the panel height.

steal: Drop a photo tile into the wordmark in place of one letter and run the lockup as a vertical reel with masked top and bottom rows.
On coloured bands, set type in a lighter tint of the band's own hue instead of white to keep the band calm.
Round only one corner of each image tile, the same corner every time, as a quiet signature shape.

name: UGLYCASH
idea: A money app sold like streetwear: one shouted condensed headline over the phone, then sticker-covered 3D props where feature icons would normally go.
hero: Near-white page. A floating light-grey nav bar only 35% of the viewport wide sits centred 20px from the top: condensed wordmark left, two social icons in the middle, an app button with a glowing magenta outline right. Directly beneath, a two-line uppercase headline in bold condensed grotesque at 11.4vw, centred, leading under 0.9, about 60% of the width, with a faint cyan and magenta fringe on the letter edges; it fills the band from 12% to 43% of the height. A single phone mockup 27% of the viewport wide rises immediately under the headline, centred, cut off by the bottom edge. Its magenta screen glow is the only colour.
type: Helvetica Now Display Condensed Bold in capitals at 164px with -0.033em tracking and very tight leading; the same face in mixed case near 34px for section headings. Inter at 14px, semi-bold, for captions. Two faces and a roughly 12:1 jump.
colour: #f7f7f7 #000000 #ffffff #ff00e6 #b6ff00 #00aeef — Off-white ground, white cards, black type. Neon magenta, lime and cyan appear only as whole-card fills, glows and stickers, never in text. Cool and synthetic overall.
imagery: Phone mockups with real app screens, plus glossy 3D props (money bags, a holographic card, an eagle, a wet-floor sign, banknotes) covered in die-cut stickers, each centred in a rounded card; some cards have grainy neon gradients.
layout: Content sits in a centred column about 60% of the viewport wide. Sections open with a left-aligned condensed heading, then rows of two or three rounded cards with captions placed outside and below. A horizontal carousel and a centred uppercase statement break the rhythm.

sections.description: A left-aligned two-line condensed heading near 34px above a row of three equal cards with 8px gaps and small radius: one pale grey with a cropped balance readout and tilted stickers, one white with two 3D money bags, one solid cyan with a phone cropped at the bottom. Captions sit beneath each card rather than inside: a bold one-word title and two short 13px lines.

Two near-square cards side by side, each half the column. Left: a grainy lime-to-lilac gradient with a white floating panel listing three rows, each with a flag, a label and a small pill button. Right: a white card with a black holographic payment card tilted about 25 degrees, stickers stuck to it. A later pair repeats the pattern with a solid magenta card holding a white icon-grid panel.

Trust carousel: a horizontal row of tall cards, each showing one 3D object centred (a chrome eagle on white, a banknote on solid lime, a yellow wet-floor sign with hand-lettered warning). The title sits inside the first card and below the others. A tiny two-dot pager is centred underneath and the next card peeks in orange at the right edge of the column.

A white rounded panel the width of the column in which the wordmark is scaled to fill the panel edge to edge, about 55% of the viewport, in black ultra-condensed capitals. Beneath it, one row with a small parent-brand credit at left and two store badges at right, then legal small print in 11px at left and four right-aligned links.

steal: Make the nav a short floating bar a third of the viewport wide so the headline can start almost at the top edge.
Replace feature icons with one photoreal 3D prop per card, each covered in die-cut stickers, and keep captions outside the card.
End with the wordmark scaled to exactly fill a white footer card, with all legal text beneath it at 11px.

name: United Carriers
idea: One operator covering every route, shown literally as a dot-matrix globe with route arcs and country tags beside a blunt three-line promise.
hero: Near-black starfield fills the viewport. A huge dot-matrix globe sits right of centre, about 90% of viewport height, bleeding off the right and bottom edges, rimmed orange on top and electric blue below, with small black country tags and orange pins. Wordmark top-left; the nav is a vertical stack of six mono links starting 29% from the left, the same x as the headline. A white pill button sits top-right under a hairline utility strip. The headline is three uppercase lines at 5.6vw in the lower half, overlapping the globe edge, with a small label above and a paragraph and two pill buttons below. The left quarter stays empty.
type: BT Steinhart bold uppercase, zero tracking, squared techno letterforms, for 80px headlines and statistic numerals over 100px. BT Steinhart Mono uppercase at about 11px for nav, tags and buttons. Helvetica Neue 13 to 16px for body. Emphasis comes from grey versus black lines, not weight changes.
colour: #060503 #ffffff #1e4bff #f26a1b #9a9a9a — Black hero and footer band, pure white body, no mid-tones. Orange and electric blue live only in the globe rim, pins and the cut-out machinery, so colour always belongs to an object.
imagery: WebGL dot-matrix globe with glowing rim and route arcs; below, a cut-out teal reach-stacker and stacked shipping containers standing on pure white; one small square-cornered aerial road thumbnail; a dot-matrix world map in the footer.
layout: An offset column about 29% from the left carries nav, headline and body, leaving the far left for the logo or small thumbnails. White sections use two columns: statement left, stacked oversized statistics right split by hairlines. Very long scroll with generous voids.

sections.description: White field, two columns. The left column holds a small square-cornered thumbnail at mid-height and, below it, a four-line uppercase statement at about 3vw whose first two lines are mid-grey and last two black. The right column stacks statistics: a one-line caption over a hairline, then a numeral around 7vw tall in heavy squared caps with a small label under it, another hairline, then the next numeral. Numerals align to the column's left edge.

Pure white section about one viewport tall containing only cut-out objects right of centre: a teal reach-stacker with its boom raised diagonally and three stacked containers in grey, navy and orange. The objects stand on the section's bottom edge, which meets a full-width black band, so the black reads as ground. No caption, card or shadow.

White footer on a faint hairline grid: tagline top-left, then a row with round social icons at left, three link columns in the middle and payment logos at right. Below, a horizontally running line of industry names in pale grey at about 1.5vw with two tiny mono tabs above it, then address blocks beside a small monochrome photo and a dot-matrix world map that echoes the hero globe.

steal: Replace the horizontal nav bar with a vertical stack of links aligned to the headline's left edge, so nav and headline form one column.
Split a statement into grey lines and black lines instead of using bold or an accent colour for emphasis.
Stand cut-out machinery on the bottom edge of a white section so the dark band that follows becomes the ground.
media: A WebGL dot-matrix globe covers the right 63% of the first screen, bleeding off the right and top edges on a black starfield, with the headline column overlapping its limb. Then a sticky stage dives through its atmosphere into the white page, and scroll-scrubbed cut-out machinery and containers stand on pure white above a black ground band that rises to become the next background, a truck holds on the seam while services scroll beneath it, and a top-down road map zooms as the vehicle turns; 34 pictures, mostly cut-outs, no video.
motion: No preloader; the hero is complete at 400ms and only the globe turns (load 11.5s in the background). Lenis and Barba drive a chain of CSS-sticky stages (16 sticky elements, no pins) scrubbed by script: the reach stacker lifts and swings, the ground band grows from 40px to 80% of the screen, the dark band moves sideways at about 1.4x scroll speed, and titles type on letter by letter with the newest letters in brand blue, mostly at .4s on the house curve cubic-bezier(.445,.05,.55,.95).

name: L.I.S.A.
idea: The agency site is replaced by a conversation with a TV-headed 3D character whose CRT face draws expressions while she types to you.
hero: A grey studio backdrop with a soft radial light fills the viewport; the whole site is this one screen. Right of centre, a 3D bust in a lilac turtleneck wears a boxy CRT television for a head, cables looping around the neck; the figure is about 83% of viewport height, cropped at the chest by the bottom edge. The TV screen shows a changing glowing shape. At left mid-height, three lines of 26px regular grotesk in black are the only copy. Top-left: wordmark and a small star-like glyph; top-right: one text link. Bottom-right: a black capsule with two sound toggles. A thin progress bar sits on the bottom edge.
type: HelveticaNowDisplay regular at one size, 26px, for wordmark, link and dialogue; earlier lines fade to pale grey and blur rather than shrinking. A block cursor follows typed text. Reply options are about 11px labels in white pills. No headline in the usual sense.
colour: #979797 #c9c9c9 #000000 #cdbfd0 #3b5bff #ffffff — A mid-grey studio gradient with black text; the only colour is the lilac sweater, blue indicator lights on the TV and chromatic fringing in the CRT glow.
imagery: One real-time 3D character: a CRT-television head with tangled cables on a mannequin torso, lit like a product shot on seamless grey. The screen displays brush-drawn white line faces, glitches and glowing eyes.
layout: A single non-scrolling screen. Text column fixed at left mid-height, character fixed at right, small utilities in the four corners. Content changes in place as the dialogue advances; mobile moves the text into a white sheet with rounded top corners rising from the bottom edge.

sections.description: Same frame, next state: the greeting stays where it was but turns pale grey and slightly blurred, and a new three-line message types in directly below it in black at the same 26px size, ending in a solid block cursor. The TV face switches to a white brush-drawn glyph, two asterisks joined by an arc, that reads as squinting eyes. A small black circular restart button appears at bottom-left.

When the message finishes, four small white pill buttons appear beneath it in two rows of two, left-aligned with the text, each roughly 110px wide with 11px labels, followed by a single line containing an underlined email address. The TV face changes to two large soft glowing circles as eyes. Nothing else enters; these pills are the entire navigation of the site.

steal: Demote earlier lines of a conversation by fading and blurring them in place instead of scrolling them away, keeping one type size throughout.
Give a 3D mascot a screen for a face so expressions can be cheap 2D line drawings rather than rigged facial animation.
Offer navigation as three or four small reply pills that appear only after the character finishes speaking.
media: One fixed full-bleed WebGL scene is the whole page: a 3D bust right of centre, about 60% of the height with the shoulders cropped by the bottom edge, whose CRT-screen face plays short clips with scanlines and glow. Corner controls sit over the render, there are no img or video elements, and on the phone the canvas sits above a white chat sheet that grows upward.
motion: Preloader lines scramble through random characters into agency descriptors, then a hard cut at about 2.5s reveals the studio scene, where the greeting types in behind random-glyph previews and a block cursor blinking on a hard 1s step. There is no document scroll: older chat lines rise and blur over 0.3s and reply pills fade and rise, mostly at .3s on the dominant ease cubic-bezier(0.215,0.61,0.355,1) (46 uses), with 5 reduced-motion rules.

name: RISK
idea: The site is a camera viewfinder: full-bleed film frames cut by glass-shard transitions, with credits, timecode and a small HUD laid over like on-monitor data.
hero: Full-bleed film frame (an athlete mid-leap against teal sky beside a stone church), sliced by faint diagonal facets that offset parts of the image. At exact centre the wordmark, heavy italic extended capitals about 270px wide, is rendered as embossed refractive glass. All text is 9 to 13px uppercase cream: three nav words top-centre; client name at the mid-left edge and project title at the mid-right edge, level with the logo; director credit bottom-left; timecode bottom-right. Two dotted vertical hairlines divide the frame into thirds. Bottom-centre, a 295x95px outlined box split into cells holds a monogram, a motto, chevrons and line glyphs, with two links joined by a rule above.
type: Syncopate bold, uppercase, slightly negative tracking, at just 9 to 13px for every label; Red Hat Display for the smallest credits. No text exceeds 0.9vw, so the only large letterforms are the glass logo. Effectively one size tier.
colour: #2c5357 #776b45 #1d3a66 #c9a06f #e8e0cc #000000 — Colour is whatever the current film frame supplies (teal skies, sandstone, skin, deep blue) under a consistent filmic grade; overlay text and lines are a single warm cream.
imagery: Full-bleed commercial film footage: sport, close-up skin, domestic interiors; low angles, motion blur, teal-and-amber grade. Transitions break the frame into angular mirrored shards. No inset images.
layout: One full-viewport frame per project in an endless vertical loop; overlay elements sit at fixed anchors (four corners, mid-left, mid-right, top-centre, bottom-centre) on a symmetric three-column guide. The layout never changes; only footage and labels swap.

sections.description: Each project reuses the hero frame exactly: new footage fills the screen, the mid-left label changes to the client, the mid-right to the film title, bottom-left to the director, and the timecode keeps counting. The glass logo stays centred and picks up the colours of whatever is behind it, rust over skin or grey-white over an interior. The outlined HUD box and nav never move.

Transition state. Between projects the image fractures into large triangular and parallelogram shards along 45-degree lines: some shards show the outgoing film, others the incoming one, slightly displaced and mirrored, so two frames coexist for a moment like light through a cut prism. The dotted verticals and cream labels stay perfectly still on top, which makes the overlay read as a fixed lens.

steal: Overlay a film reel with fixed viewfinder data (credits at the edges, timecode in a corner, dotted third-lines) so project metadata feels like camera information.
Render the logo as transparent refractive glass over the footage so it takes its colour from every frame instead of having one.
Keep every overlay element at one tiny size and anchor each to a corner or edge midpoint, leaving the centre of the frame to the picture.
media: Footage is the whole site: one fixed full-screen WebGL stage plays six commercial films in turn, each covering 100% of the screen under a uniform dark overlay, with a glass wordmark about 20% of the width at dead centre refracting the film and 45-degree glass shards cutting into the frame. No img or video elements; labels sit at the four edges.
motion: An intro of about 2s: a moving gradient field with the wordmark and a counter that travels from the bottom-right to the top-right corner as it reaches 100. Lenis drives an endless reel over a document about 540,000px tall that starts in the middle, each 900px wheel step cutting to the next film with no pins or section changes, while labels rise 30px when they change (twelve GSAP y tweens) and the CSS has no cubic-beziers at all.

name: PROOOOF
idea: The product's output is the page: a wall of photos each wearing its coloured EXIF strip, with all the copy folded into one small floating card.
hero: The whole viewport is a six-column masonry of photographs on a warm off-white ground with about 15px gutters, columns offset vertically so rows never line up. Each photo has a flat strip fused to its bottom edge carrying tiny monospaced capture data, every strip a different solid colour (black, red, orange, yellow, violet, green). Dead centre floats a white card about 380px wide and 410px tall with roughly 28px corner radius and a soft shadow. It contains an extended wordmark with chained O's, a two-row accordion with the first row open, an App Store badge and a monospaced line of links. There is no navigation.
type: An extended, heavy wordmark with interlocked O's is the only display type. Card text is Wintyr VF at about 14-16px, medium weight for accordion headings. EXIF strips and footer links are monospace at roughly 8-13px. No headline anywhere.
colour: #f3eee9 #fafafa #191818 #ff6a2b #f7c531 #5a4fcf — Colour comes from the photographs and the saturated caption strips, one hue per photo. Card and gutters stay off-white; a final panel flips to near-black with grey characters.
imagery: Casual travel, food, pet and concert photos in mixed portrait and landscape crops, square corners, ungraded, tiled edge to edge. The page ends on an ASCII-art rendering of a hand holding a camera.
layout: Effectively a single screen: the photo wall sits behind a centred card that carries every word. Six columns on desktop, two on mobile where the card widens to nearly full width. The only second scene is a dark, inset ASCII panel.

sections.description: All product copy lives in the centred card as an accordion: a row with heading left and chevron right, a hairline divider, the open panel's four-line paragraph, a centred store badge, another divider, a collapsed second row, then a small monospaced line with a version number and underlined links. The card stays put while the wall remains visible on all four sides.

Each tile is a photo with a data strip attached below: two or three rows of monospaced text, four values spread evenly across the first row, date and time at opposite ends of the second, maker and model on the third. Strip and text colours change per tile, for example yellow on black, black on yellow, white on violet, so a uniform grid looks varied.

The closing panel is a near-black rectangle inset with wide margins and filled edge to edge with rows of grey ASCII characters that resolve into a picture of a hand gripping a camera. One line of tiny monospaced uppercase text sits at the exact centre as the call to action. No button and no logo.

steal: Show the product's output at wall scale as the background and confine all copy to one small card on top of it.
Give every repeated tile its own flat accent colour for the caption strip so a strict grid reads as lively.
Hold the explanatory copy in an accordion inside the hero card so the page needs no scrolling.

name: Artem Shcherbakov
idea: A director's reel hides behind a small pill-shaped window that scrolls open to fill the screen, while neon-green marker scribbles deface the polite typography.
hero: White page. Three nav words are pinned to the very top: one hard left, the name centred, one hard right, in bold condensed lowercase about 28px, touching the edges. The content is a single horizontal row at mid-height in three equal parts. Left: a two-line greeting in an ultra-heavy rounded sans at about 6vw, with a neon-green hand-scrawled word and underline drawn over it. Centre: a vertical rounded-rectangle window about 180 by 300px showing zoomed, pixelated video. Right: a green doodle face above a centred six-line bio at about 22px. A tiny grey scroll cue sits bottom-centre. More than 60% is white.
type: EaseDouble at weight 900 with -0.08em tracking, letters nearly fused, for display; plain Arial Narrow for nav and body, bold in the nav. About 88px display against roughly 22px body. Display type melts into soft blobs between states.
colour: #ffffff #0e0e0e #17e84a #ff2ecb — Black on white, inverting to white on near-black for the footer. One neon green is reserved for hand-drawn scribbles and doodles, with a single touch of magenta.
imagery: CG character footage treated with scanlines, colour fringing and heavy pixelation, shown first inside a small pill mask and then full-bleed. Crude marker doodles (faces, robot, clapperboard) in green outline are scattered around it.
layout: A short single-scroll sequence: three-part intro row, full-bleed video with a stacked project list, a centred paragraph in display type, a dark contact panel. Nav words stay in the top corners throughout. No grid lines, no cards, no section headings.

sections.description: The video fills the viewport edge to edge. Project names are stacked bottom-left in the heavy rounded face at about 5vw, lowercase with tight leading, in translucent white so footage shows through; the active name turns solid white and gets a green scribble across it. The list runs off the bottom edge. In a later state the video shrinks to a rounded rectangle about two-thirds of the viewport wide.

A centred five-line paragraph set entirely in the 900-weight rounded display face at about 4.5vw on white, tracked so tightly the letters touch. The last line is caught mid-reveal as soft black blobs, showing that each line condenses from a blurred, gooey state into legible type.

Near-black panel. A two-line centred heading in white display type sits at the top with green and magenta scribbles over a few letters. Below, a narrow centred column lists contact details in small plain sans, each preceded by a tiny grey label. Five or six green line doodles are scattered around the edges, some cropped by the viewport.

steal: Start the showreel as a small pill-shaped mask in the hero and let scrolling grow it to full-bleed.
Overdraw clean display type with a single-colour hand scribble to add personality without a second typeface.
Pair one extravagant display face with a deliberately default system face (Arial Narrow) for everything functional.
media: The first screen is white type with almost no picture. From the first scroll step a project reel drawn into a WebGL canvas with a scanline and colour-fringe shader covers the whole screen behind a giant credit list, then shrinks to a centred rounded card of about 720x880, and later a black pill rises and grows into a full dark panel ringed by green line doodles, all without a video element in the DOM.
motion: A tiny percentage counter runs about 4.5s, stalling at 54 for over a second, then the nav and role line sharpen from blur (filter .7s, opacity 1.2s, cubic-bezier(.33,1,.68,1)). Custom smooth scroll pins the footage while the credit list rises over it, the frame contracts into a card, manifesto words go from blur to sharp in scroll order, and a pill expands by clip-path into the contact panel; display type melts through a goo threshold before it sets.

name: Builders Table
idea: A conference page laid out like a creative-coding workspace: generative canvases sit on a dot grid inside selection boxes with file-name tags and a live control panel.
hero: Charcoal page with a faint dot grid. A hairline-underlined tab bar with two text tabs runs across the top. Next row: stacked-caps wordmark at the 40px left margin, date and venue in two grey lines at 55% with a small lime square bullet, a lime rectangular button far right. The headline is two lines of uppercase grotesk at about 5.5vw, left-aligned, first line white, second mid-grey, followed by a two-line grey paragraph and two buttons. The lower 40% holds four outlined canvases at different sizes and heights, each with white corner handles and a tiny coloured mono tag: a plus-sign field, green smoke, a cyan dot-matrix portrait, a slider panel.
type: Laygrotesk at weight 400 for everything: uppercase headlines between 5.5vw and 7vw with very tight leading and a white/grey split per line, 20px body with a tight letterfit, plus tiny mono caps for file tags, label rows and footer links.
colour: #111111 #ffffff #dafa9c #000000 #5fb6d9 #8f8f8f — Charcoal hero, white middle sections, black footer. Pale lime is the single action colour on every button and tag; cyan, magenta and green appear only inside the generative canvases.
imagery: Shader and dither canvases: grids of plus signs, green noise clouds, portraits rebuilt from coloured dots. Framed with one-pixel outlines, square corner handles and file-name labels, as if selected in a design tool.
layout: 40px margins, everything hung from the left edge. Dark hero with scattered frames, then orderly white sections, each opened by a three-part mono label row over a hairline and a two-line two-tone heading; schedule and speaker lists use a sidebar-plus-rows structure.

sections.description: Three equal dark tiles in a row, about 310px tall with 8px gaps, each filled with a different generative texture (plus-sign grid, magenta dither, blurred blue-grey bars). Each carries three lines of small white text anchored bottom-left with 16px padding. No icons or headings: the texture is the differentiator. The row sits directly under a white intro block with a large left paragraph and small right paragraph.

A label row of three tiny mono words (left, centre, right) over a hairline, then a two-line uppercase heading, first line grey, second black, with a lime button on the same row at far right. Below: a 130px left column of two stacked day tabs, the active one black, and a right column of pale-grey rows, each with time at 20px, a small grey meta line, the title in a second column and overlapping round avatars far right.

A black panel set over the last strip of dot grid, with canvas frames peeking above it. Top-left a short-form wordmark with the year at about 6vw; top-right a three-row accordion with bracketed mono numbers, 20px labels and plus signs, separated by hairlines. Bottom-left a two-line tagline; bottom-right a column of tiny mono legal links; a final mono caps line spans the base.

steal: Frame generative visuals with selection handles and a tiny file-name tag so decoration reads as work in progress.
Split a two-line uppercase headline into two tones, one line full strength and one grey, instead of changing size or weight.
Replace icon feature cards with tiles whose only differentiator is a distinct generative texture, text pinned bottom-left.

name: NOTHIN’
idea: The studio's name set as a wordmark so large it is the whole hero, repeated in inverted colours as the footer, so 'nothing' is literally the only content on screen.
hero: The captured hero frame is a black preloader wipe; this describes the loaded state. White field. A custom heavy geometric wordmark in black spans the full width between 1% margins, vertically centred, about 30% of the viewport tall, its apostrophe hanging at the top-right. Top-left: a two-line statement at about 1.6vw with a small black pill button under it. Top-right: a tiny menu label with a four-dot icon. Along the bottom edge: a one-line studio descriptor at left, two social links and a language chip at right. Everything else is empty white, with no image and no colour.
type: PP Neue Montreal medium for statements at up to about 5vw, sentence case, tight tracking and leading; the Book cut for small text; IBM Plex Mono for tiny grey project labels. The wordmark is custom heavy geometric lettering at close to 100vw. Only three text sizes: statement, caption, micro-label.
colour: #ffffff #000000 #2b47e6 #2f5d33 #bfbfbf — Strict black and white that flips by section: white hero and intro, black works and footer. The only colour comes from inside the imagery, chiefly electric-blue foil and fern green.
imagery: 3D renders of inflated chrome, crumpled blue foil and bubble-wrap hearts on black; project shots are brand mock-ups photographed in settings (a card among ferns, a laptop on a dark desk). Hard-edged rectangles of varied size, square corners.
layout: Margins of about 1%, so content runs nearly edge to edge. The intro is a left headline over a full-width black media panel; the works section places images at irregular widths and horizontal offsets with wide black gaps, each with a mono label and one-line caption above.

sections.description: White section. A two-line statement at about 5vw sits flush left under a small logo mark, filling the top quarter. Below it a black rectangle spans the full content width and runs off the bottom of the viewport, holding a 3D still life clustered at centre. On further scroll the panel shrinks to a small thumbnail docked top-right, while a parenthesised label and a four-line paragraph at caption size appear in two narrow columns at the left.

Black section headed by one bold uppercase word top-left. Project images are placed as a loose scatter: one at about 48% width hugging the left margin, the next narrow and hugging the right margin lower down, the next inset to start 18% across. Above each image sits a tiny grey mono project name, then a one-line white caption at about 1.1vw. A two-line aphorism floats alone at the right between projects. Long stretches of empty black separate items.

Black, full viewport. A two-line invitation at about 5vw at the left in the upper third, with two outlined pill buttons under it; three social links stacked at about 78% across. The wordmark repeats in white at full width, anchored to the bottom, with a single row of micro-text credits beneath it.

steal: Make the hero nothing but the name: a wordmark scaled to the full viewport width on a blank field, with only a two-line statement and one small button in a corner.
Repeat the hero wordmark in inverted colours as the footer so the page opens and closes on the same shape.
Place case-study images at different widths and horizontal offsets on a black field, each with a micro mono label and a single-line caption above it instead of a card.
media: No picture on the desktop first screen: a full-width black wordmark on white covers about 30% of the height. Then an inset showreel with 18px gutters scrubs down into a box in the right third as text arrives on the left, a staggered two-column mosaic of 48, 32 and 65% widths, a pinned full-bleed brand film with a blurred copy behind it as a halo, cut-out 3D objects on black with letters tumbling between them, and the wordmark again, inverted, as the footer; 17 images and 4 muted looping videos.
motion: The preloader (on the phone capture) morphs a 3D inflatable through three forms while a counter runs down to 000, then white rises in a hard-edged mask to reveal the wordmark. Lenis: the showreel scrubs at 3, works cards drift at their own speeds (y scrub 1.5, yPercent scrub 3), the film pins for one screen, heading letters split and scatter, and services letters and objects tumble in on power2.in at random 0.25-0.69s durations; the house ease is cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) at 0.5-0.6s.

name: Superlocal 2026
idea: Everything is a circle: a dot-matrix logotype whose dots become floating photo circles and glowing orbs across a grey-to-orange field.
hero: Mid-grey field with a faint dot grid (one dot every 33px) that fades through the lower half into saturated orange at the bottom edge. The captured first paint contains one element: a 270×80px logotype dead centre, built from black ellipses of varying size, its letters progressively compressed to the right. No nav or text yet. After loading, a cluster of four small pills (one black, three white) appears top-centre; the logo turns white inside a 330px ring of about fifty tiny circles — round photo crops, glowing orbs, coins; and the bottom edge carries the event name left and dates right in an outlined dot-matrix face 40px tall.
type: Display text is an outlined dot-matrix face drawn on canvas, about 40px caps, modules flickering. All other text is one tight bold grotesk ('fontSans') from 12 to 24px with negative tracking. The logotype is built from ellipses on the same matrix.
colour: #bcbcbc #ff641e #1a1302 #ffb740 #c13bff #ffffff — Every screen repeats a vertical fade from flat grey to hot orange. Orbs add magenta-violet cores; the footer swaps to a soft yellow glow. Text is near-black, nav pills black and white.
imagery: Event photographs cropped to circles from 60 to 240px, floating without a grid alongside hard-edged radial-gradient orbs and coin images; some pairs overlap. The logo and footer art are generated dot matrices.
layout: No visible grid: circles drift across each screen while text locks to the bottom corners (statement bottom-left, description bottom-right). A four-pill nav stays top-centre. The footer resolves into three text columns over a screen-filling dot-matrix glow.

sections.description: No grid. Circular photo crops between 60 and 240px across float over the grey-to-orange field, a few overlapping in pairs. A flat radial orb (orange rim, magenta-violet core, about 160px) sits among them and others are cut by the viewport edges. The pill nav stays top-centre; nothing else is fixed.

Bottom-left: a small bold date line, then a two-line statement in the outlined dot-matrix face at about 36px, some modules lit orange mid-animation. Bottom-right: a two-line 12px bold description. Above them three photo circles (190px portrait near centre, poster collage left, stage shot right) and a large orb top-right.

Grey field with a huge soft yellow radial glow. The dot-matrix logo is enlarged to fill the screen, its ellipses knocked out of the yellow in grey. On top: three columns of bold 18px text (contact message and email left, press list centre, socials right), a tiny credits list, and a bottom line with dates, year and city in the same three columns.

steal: Build the logotype from a dot matrix of ellipses of varying size, then reuse the same matrix at screen-filling scale as the footer background.
Crop every photo to a circle at wildly different diameters and let them float with coloured orbs instead of sitting in a gallery grid.
Fade each screen from flat grey into one saturated colour at its bottom edge so the viewport itself carries the brand colour.

name: Produx Design
idea: The wordmark is the hero, and the showreel image assembles itself from scattered square fragments as you scroll.
hero: Near-black field with 80px side margins. The wordmark, in a wide, light-weight uppercase sans with a slashed O, runs margin to margin (about 89% of the width) with a cap height near 20% of the viewport, starting 9% from the top. A large empty gap follows. In the lower half a two-line statement at 5.1vw sits flush left; opposite it, bottom-aligned to the statement and flush to the right margin, is a three-line paragraph in small monospace about a quarter of the width. No nav bar, button or image in the first viewport; the bottom quarter is empty.
type: At Aero in light-to-medium weight for the wordmark, the 74px statement and project titles; DM Mono for the hero paragraph, bracketed nav items and uppercase project blurbs at about 11px. Three sizes; the statement is roughly five times the mono text.
colour: #0e0e0e #e4e4e4 #545e54 #303930 #6f8f3a — Near-black page with off-white type and no accent colour. Colour arrives only through imagery: moss green and sage in the showreel render, then each case-study thumbnail brings its own palette.
imagery: A 3D render of a moss-covered boulder on a sage background, first broken into scattered square tiles, then whole as a 16:9 inset. Work thumbnails are square-cornered stills and video in mixed ratios, including one vivid orange-violet gradient card.
layout: 80px margins. After the hero, a small logo top-left and four bracketed mono links spread across the right half. Hero is all type, the next three screens are a pinned image assembly, then a work grid with unequal column widths and mono captions under each thumbnail.

sections.description: Pinned showreel reveal on black. Eight to ten small square tiles, 60 to 100px, each a different crop of the same image, float scattered around the centre at different depths, some blurred. As scroll advances they multiply, enlarge and lock together until they form one 16:9 image inset at about 70% of viewport width, with the wordmark centred on it in white and tiny captions overlaid at left and lower right.

Two unequal columns on black, roughly 52% and 30% of the width with a wide gutter. Each item is a square-cornered thumbnail with a row of small rectangular mono tags along its bottom edge; beneath it a small square bullet, the project name in the sans at about 16px and a two-line uppercase mono blurb. The next item breaks the grid: a single thumbnail centred at about 75% width.

steal: Run the wordmark margin to margin in a light weight rather than a heavy one; thin strokes at huge size read as assured instead of loud.
Pair one large sans statement with a tiny monospace paragraph bottom-aligned on the opposite margin and leave the middle of the row empty.
Introduce the hero image as scattered square crops of itself that converge into the full frame on scroll.
media: The fold has no media at all; the first picture is the 40s showreel, which arrives on the second screen as scattered square tiles at different depths that converge into an inset 16:9 frame, then fills 56-96% of each screen until it is full-bleed at about 4850px. Below: a staggered two-column mosaic with a centred wide interlude, a logo strip bleeding off both edges, and a pinned 3D stone centre-right with the statement docked bottom-left; zero radius everywhere.
motion: Black at 400ms, then wordmark letters rise one by one out of a baseline mask, tagline words rise in masked lines and the small blurb types itself out, settled by about 2.2s. Lenis drives a sticky, scrubbed hero in which tiles fly in from depth, blurred to sharp, assemble the frame and scale it to full bleed, then headings resolve through a pixel-slice glitch, work frames reveal by inset clip, the manifesto colours word by word and the closing stone grows moss as the ground turns from black to moss green, all as per-frame script (44,246 style mutations) with no GSAP exposed.

name: Kononenko Architectural Bureau
idea: Let the renders do the talking: one full-bleed visualisation, a name set half in grotesk and half in serif, then alternating oversized sans and serif statements on white.
hero: A single architectural render fills the viewport edge to edge: a low grey metal-clad building under a large overcast sky, wild grass across the bottom third. Type is white and tiny except for the name. Top-left at a 24px margin, the bureau name is stacked on three lines at 13px. Top-right, four links run inline separated by commas, the current one underlined. Bottom-left, the name repeats at 60px (4.2vw) on two tight lines, the first two words in grotesk and the last word in a serif at the same size. No button, no scrim, no tagline; the sky takes the upper 45% untouched.
type: Two faces (digest names are obfuscated): a tight neo-grotesk at −0.03em and a soft high-contrast serif, mixed inside one line in the name. Section statements alternate: centred sans at about 6.5vw, then left-aligned serif at 4.5vw with a first-line indent. Labels are 9px.
colour: #ffffff #000000 #b7b7b9 #7c8050 #3d3a36 #9a9a9a — White pages with black type; colour comes only from the renders' overcast greys, greens and dark timber. The footer inverts to solid black with white letters.
imagery: Photoreal architectural visualisations in muted natural light, shown full-bleed at wide panoramic crops with square corners and no overlays; one loose black ink sketch on white stands in for process.
layout: 24px outer margins. Full-bleed image bands alternate with white type-only screens. Big statements either centre or run the full width; small data sits in narrow columns with tiny serif labels left of sans values, and hairline tables are inset to the right-hand third.

sections.description: White screen with a two-line sans heading centred at roughly 6.5vw, tight leading, taking the top third. Directly beneath, two tiny grey captions of two lines each sit side by side, each about 130px wide, centred as a pair. A full-bleed panoramic render starts immediately below and runs off the bottom, so the heading reads as a caption to the picture.

Far left, three label and value pairs at 9px (serif label, sans value) stack in a 150px column. From 34% across, a five-line serif paragraph at about 22px runs to 90% of the width. 120px lower a second row repeats the logic for achievements: a label at far left, then two narrow list columns of awards and publications at 9px with generous gaps between them.

A four-line serif statement at 4.5vw spans the full width, left-aligned with the first line indented about 3% and leading under 1. Below it, pushed into the right-hand 35% of the page, an offices table: a tiny label hangs to its left, and each row holds office type, country and city in grey, an address, and a small arrow, divided by hairlines at 18px row height.

Solid black. A top band of five tiny columns (name, navigation, media, address, hours), each a grey label beside a white list. Then a four-letter abbreviation of the name in white grotesk fills the entire width, letters about 45% of the viewport tall and touching both edges, with a single 8px legal line squeezed beneath.

steal: Set the last word of a sans headline in an upright serif of the same size to give a plain name a signature without any graphic device.
Alternate statement voices down the page: a centred grotesk heading, then a full-width left-aligned serif paragraph at display size with a first-line indent.
Close with an abbreviation of the name scaled until it touches both edges of a black footer, with all practical links shrunk to 9px above it.
media: One photoreal render covers the whole first screen with only the title docked bottom-left and no scrim. Below: a full-bleed 2:1 band under a centred headline, overscanned 32px per side for parallax, a staggered two-column scatter of landscape and portrait frames at uneven offsets, hand sketches drawn into the white page between statements, and a ring of small rotated square team photographs round a centred headline on black; 27 images and a fixed WebGL layer, no video.
motion: A white preloader with a progress line along the top and a counter stalled near 60 for 2.5s; by 4.5s the hero is in and the title rises out of a mask line by line. Lenis over the fixed WebGL layer: sketches build stroke by stroke on a scrub, the ground flips white to black over 0.3s at the values chapter, paragraph lines rise over 0.5s, and team photographs spiral in and settle into a ring; one ease for everything, cubic-bezier(.17,.84,.44,1), 34 uses.

name: Studio K95
idea: The whole portfolio is one WebGL room: project images orbit in rings around a chrome voxel rose inside an electric-blue gridded cylinder.
hero: A saturated ultramarine field covers the viewport, drawn with a faint dark grid that curves as if seen from inside a cylinder. At centre floats a chrome, stair-stepped 3D rose about 57% of the viewport height. Around it some twenty project images sit as upright planes on three horizontal rings: stamp-sized along the top and bottom, two large portrait ones flanking the rose, each angled toward the centre. Interface text is tiny and pinned to the edges with 58px margins: logo top left, a pill layout toggle top centre, three caps links and a language switch top right; a discipline line, a works counter and the year along the bottom.
type: One wide-set grotesk ('adaptive' in the digest) at a single small size, roughly 14 to 16px, bold, caps for nav and labels. No display headline is shown; the digest's 32px heading is not visible. The blocky geometric logo is the only large letterform.
colour: #0800b7 #1500e1 #c8ccd4 #ffffff #e9e34a #e23a28 — One electric blue fills everything; white type and chrome geometry sit on it, and every other colour arrives through the project thumbnails. A single yellow dot marks the cursor.
imagery: Project stills (posters, packaging, furniture, brand marks) as square-cornered portrait planes in 3D perspective, uncropped and ungraded, plus a reflective chrome voxel rose as the centre object.
layout: A single non-scrolling screen. Content lives in 3D space while a thin heads-up frame holds three items across the top and three across the bottom, with nothing between them but the canvas. Scrolling rotates the scene rather than moving the page.

sections.description: The index is the scene itself. Scrolling or dragging spins the rings so different thumbnails swing to the front and scale up to roughly 40% of viewport height, while the rest recede to stamp size at the edges and corners. Hovering a plane attaches a small translucent pill to the cursor with an arrow, the project name and its discipline. A segmented pill at top centre switches the arrangement between rings and a spiral.

There is no footer block, only a single baseline 30px above the bottom edge carrying three items in the same small bold type: the studio's discipline flush left, a counter of shown versus total projects at centre with one underlined word linking to the full list, and the copyright year flush right. Thumbnails pass behind this line as the scene turns.

steal: Let a single saturated colour field be the whole page and take every other colour from the work thumbnails.
Offer two named arrangements of the same index through a small segmented toggle, so the layout itself becomes a control.
Keep interface text to one small size pinned at the corners and centre edges, including a live count of shown versus total projects.
media: WebGL covers the whole fold: about 25-30 portrait project cards (3:4, square corners, shown as photographed) on three rings round the camera, roughly 35-40% of the pixels, round a central chrome rose (about 15%), on a gridded ultramarine field. The focused card is pulled to the front at about 3x its neighbours' size, and a glass label beside the cursor names it; no DOM images and no video.
motion: Readable in about 1.2s with no preloader: the canvas fades in over 0.7s ease and the label switches from a scroll prompt to the focused project by 2.5s. The page never scrolls: the wheel, smoothed by Lenis, turns the card rings round the camera while the rose spins from face-on to edge-on about every two steps, as continuous inertial rotation with no reveals, and label lines enter over 0.95s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), with cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) and (.4,0,.2,1) as the house eases and 9 reduced-motion queries.

name: Julien Calot
idea: Each series of paintings is a full-screen close crop of one canvas, with the series title, year and piece count strung along a single line at mid-height like a museum wall label.
hero: A painting detail fills the viewport edge to edge, a face in the centre with saturated landscape shapes around it and the canvas weave visible. All text is white and small, with no scrim. Top-left: the artist's name in bold condensed capitals about 45px tall, the largest type on screen. The same top row holds a two-item filter at 29% across and two small stacked link groups at 75% and 95%. On the vertical midline a single row reads: year at the far left, series title in condensed black caps at 1.6vw about 10% in, and a piece count preceded by a short dash at the far right. No button.
