hero: Light grey field with soft darker blurs toward the corners. A steel chronograph rendered in 3D stands upright at dead centre, about 80% of viewport height. Behind it the product name is set once across the full width in a wide, squared geometric sans at 24vw in mid-grey; the watch covers the middle character, so only two letters at the left edge and two at the right are readable. A thin circle about 700px across with faint radial spokes and one darker arc sits behind the watch like a dial diagram. No navigation, logo, body copy or button anywhere.
type: Nekst, a wide squared geometric sans, regular weight, uppercase, used only huge (up to 25vw) in black, mid-grey and white within one line stack. Body is Inter at 12px in 130px columns, roughly a 30x jump with nothing in between.
colour: #e8e8e8 #c7c7c7 #a1a1a1 #6b6b6b #0a0a0a #ffffff — Entirely greyscale: pale grey ground with out-of-focus darker clouds, type in black, grey and white. The page darkens to mid-grey for the exploded view. Only the brass gear train adds warmth.
imagery: One real-time 3D steel watch shown front, three-quarter, caseback and exploded into dial, movement and plates lined up on a horizontal axis. No photographs; the object floats with no ground shadow.
layout: No grid chrome at all: the object holds the centre while type moves around it. Giant letters crop at any edge, captions sit in a 130px column left or right of the watch, and one product label is rotated 90 degrees.

sections.description: Four stacked lines of uppercase display type about 110px tall, flush left at mid-page and running off the right edge: line one mid-grey, line two black, lines three and four pale grey to white. The watch, tilted three-quarter, floats over the upper right of the stack and hides parts of letters, so type and object share the same space instead of sitting side by side.

The watch is turned to show its open caseback, placed just left of centre. To its right, a 130px-wide column holds two micro-paragraphs at 12px, each with a grey one-line title above. A small grey circular toggle sits far left. A white display word crops off the top edge. The rest of the frame is empty grey with a darker blurred cloud at upper right.

Exploded view. The ground shifts to a mid-grey vertical gradient with a faint horizon line. The watch's components (dial, tourbillon, movement, barrel, bridges) are separated and spaced along one horizontal axis at eye level like specimens. Tiny part names are set vertically along the bottom edge under each piece; a small prompt with a plus icon sits top-centre.

steal: Set the product name so large that the product itself replaces one of its characters, leaving the name half-hidden and the object as the missing letter.
Stack one display line in three tints (black, mid-grey, white) on a grey ground so a single typeface produces depth without colour.
End a product story with an exploded view laid out on one horizontal axis with vertical micro-labels instead of a spec table.
media: One fixed full-bleed WebGL canvas renders every picture: a steel chronograph about 620px tall (69% of the height, 29% of the width) centred inside a 720px ring with the giant model code behind it, then the watch from every side, an exploded line of parts on an axis with leader labels, particle ribbons on black, a black-finish reprise and a close-up cropped by the bottom edge. No photographs and no video; two very tall gradient overlays hand the ground from light to dark and back.
motion: The preloader holds at least 4.5s on the 3D assets, then its 720px circle stays to become the ring round the watch while a dark arc draws clockwise over 1.2s. Lenis drives one pinned, scrubbed timeline over 38 screens: the watch turns, separates into parts, the ground moves from #ebebeb to #a1a1a1 to #0a0a0a, and headline lines change colour by their distance from the viewport centre; per-character transforms are written every frame, smoothed by a 20ms ease-out.

name: Justin Lerner
idea: The portfolio is a hairline grid of square cells in which the letters of the owner's name are scattered among small animated project emblems, so name and work form one crossword-like board.
hero: White page divided by pale grey hairlines into five columns of exact squares (each 20vw), so three full rows and a sliver of a fourth show. No header, navigation or text block. Each cell holds one centred object about half the cell wide: either a single black slab-serif capital at 5.6vw (one in the top-left cell, one top-right, three more scattered through rows two and three) or a small project emblem such as a pixel speech bubble, a photographed bowl, a red robot arm, a wireframe figure, a logo badge or a line-drawn building. One cell holds only a soft blurred cloud. About 90% of the area is white.
type: Museo Slab is the only face on desktop: weight-500 capitals at 80px used as grid letters, with no body copy at all (eleven words on the page). Mobile adds light italic slab project names and small sans year tabs.
colour: #ffffff #e9eae8 #111111 #fff200 #f0563a #4fd0c8 — White ground, grey hairlines, black letters. Colour arrives only in the emblems, each in its own one- or two-colour scheme (yellow, coral, teal, purple). Mobile adds two solid yellow icon tiles.
imagery: Small spot illustrations and logos in deliberately mixed styles (pixel art, line drawing, isometric, wireframe mesh, one cut-out photo), each centred in a square cell with no frame or background, and animated.
layout: A single edge-to-edge grid of 20vw squares with hairline dividers and no outer margin; the whole site is about 1.3 screens. Mobile switches to two columns and adds a year tab in each cell's top-right corner and an italic name under each emblem.

sections.description: The grid continues for one more row below the fold with five cells holding only emblems. Across frames the emblems are caught in different states: a logo badge collapsing to a small monogram, a scan line moving down the wireframe figure, a pencil travelling across a drawn face, a coin appearing and disappearing. Each cell is a tiny looping or hover-driven animation, with no captions on desktop.

Mobile header built from the same cells: a small square with the initial on crosshair lines at left, an empty cell, then two solid-yellow square tiles carrying a document icon and a paper-plane icon. Below, the two-column grid gives each project a boxed year tab notched into the top-right corner of its cell and an italic slab project name near the bottom, sometimes overlapping the emblem.

steal: Spell the name by dropping its letters into scattered cells of a hairline grid and fill the remaining cells with project marks, so identity and index share one structure.
Give each project a single small animated emblem centred in a large empty square instead of a screenshot thumbnail.
On mobile, notch a small boxed year tab into the corner of each grid cell and label the cell with an italic name at its base.

name: Monte
idea: No real concept: one warm interior photograph sells the venue while a booking bar stays pinned to the bottom of every screen.
hero: An interior photograph fills the viewport edge to edge down to a 70px full-width taupe bar pinned at the bottom, which carries a single centred serif booking link. The venue name sits alone at the exact centre of the image in a light serif at about 4vw, white, with no subhead and no button. A transparent header overlays the top: the parent group's logo at a 40px left margin, seven sans links spread along the right half, divided from the image by a one-pixel translucent rule. There is no scrim; the photo's warm mid-tones carry the white text. Mobile keeps the same arrangement with a hamburger.
type: Domaine Text Light for the venue name, intro paragraphs, section titles and footer links, all modest (60px name, 28 to 40px elsewhere); Modern Gothic for navigation, labels and small print at 12 to 16px. No large display type anywhere: the scale is deliberately flat.
colour: #f5f0ea #b9b1a4 #000000 #b5694d #ddd8d2 — Warm cream page, a taupe booking bar, black for the gift-card panel and footer. Colour comes from the photography: terracotta tile, pale timber and plant green.
imagery: Editorial interior and food photography in warm natural light, often with a motion-blurred figure. Full-bleed hero, then a horizontal strip of mixed-width crops, square social thumbnails and tall 4:5 venue portraits; corners almost square.
layout: 40px side margins with content hung from full-width hairlines. Text-and-details rows alternate with image carousels that bleed off the right edge; a black inset panel and a black footer break the cream. The taupe booking bar persists at the bottom of every screen.

sections.description: Cream band opened by a full-width hairline. Left: a five-line serif paragraph at about 28px occupying roughly 48% of the width. Right third: a details table of six rows (hours, address, phone, email, social, website), each a small grey label with its value indented about 115px, separated by hairlines. Directly below, a strip of photographs of unequal widths runs off the right edge, cropped by the viewport.

A black rectangle inset 40px from the page edges and about 650px tall. Left of centre, a six-line serif paragraph in cream at about 30px with a tiny outlined pill button under it; at right, a single flat taupe rectangle the proportions of a bank card, about 235px wide, bearing the logo split to its two edges. Nothing else: the flat card stands in for an image.

A horizontal carousel of sibling venues: 4:5 portrait photographs about 440px wide with 20px gaps, three visible and a fourth peeking at the right edge. Under each: the venue name in roughly 40px serif, generous space, a hairline, a small bold 'view venue' label, a two-line description in 14px sans and an outlined pill booking button.

steal: Pin a full-width, low booking bar in a muted brand tone to the bottom of the viewport instead of placing a button in the hero.
Set the venue name small (about 4vw) and dead-centre on an unscrimmed photograph and let the image supply the scale.
Present practical details as a label and value table with hairline separators beside the intro paragraph rather than as icon rows.

name: TAB Kitchen & Bakery
idea: A scroll-driven walk into a flat-colour illustrated cafe: a line of text parts to reveal an oval vignette that grows until you are standing inside the room.
hero: A full-viewport brick-red field carrying nothing but type. The three-word name is centred horizontally and sits just above vertical centre in a light regular serif at 6.3vw with very wide word spaces, cream on red. Directly beneath is a cream rule about 4px thick, exactly as wide as the title, then a one-line subtitle at roughly a third of the title size, also centred. No navigation, logo, button or image; about 85% of the screen is empty colour. It works as a title card before the scroll sequence starts.
type: Inria Serif regular for the opening title at 90px; PP Editorial New, light and slightly condensed, for the dark-green scroll lines at about 4vw; Sometype Mono in uppercase for the two corner labels and footer credits at about 12px. Three sizes in total.
colour: #9c4f49 #f7e5cd #34492d #7a7a4f #efb55b #1c1c1c — Each scroll chapter is a flat field: brick red, then cream, with olive and mustard later. Type is cream on red and dark leaf-green on cream; the illustrations use the same four hues. Warm throughout.
imagery: Flat vector illustration with black keylines in four colours: a cafe interior with red cabinet and lantern, shown first inside an outlined oval, then full-bleed; olive leaf sprigs cropped by the side edges; a botanical footer frieze with a dog.
layout: One idea per screen across about 26 pinned screens. Two tiny mono labels fixed in the top corners are the only persistent chrome; everything else is centred type or a single illustration on a flat field with wide empty margins.

sections.description: Cream field. Two centred lines of light serif at about 4vw in dark green. On scroll they separate diagonally, the first line sliding up and left and the second down and right, while a horizontal oval with a double black outline, about 40% of viewport width, opens between them showing the cafe illustration. Large olive leaf sprigs enter from the left and right edges and are cropped by the viewport.

The oval scales up until the illustration fills the viewport edge to edge: a one-point-perspective room in flat brick, olive, mustard and cream with black outlines, a counter in the left foreground, a carved cabinet on the far wall and red shelving at the right edge. The two corner mono labels stay on top of the artwork; there is no other text.

Pale cream field. A symmetrical band of sage-and-peach botanical illustration spans the full width across the middle third, with the small serif logo inside a vine cartouche centred above a tan dog. Two single-line mono credits in brick red sit at the bottom-left and bottom-right corners. No link columns, no rule, no background block.

steal: Open with a chrome-free title card: one serif line, a rule exactly the title's width and a subtitle, centred on a flat saturated field.
Split a two-line statement diagonally on scroll, reveal an image in the gap, then scale that image's mask until it becomes the next full-bleed scene.
Hold illustration, type and backgrounds to the same four flat hues so each section change is a palette swap rather than a new style.

name: Lacoste Ace Breaker
idea: A branded arcade-game title screen where the game's own paddle and ball are set into the lockup like punctuation, over a dimmed 3D tennis court.
hero: Single fixed screen. A dimmed, slowly drifting 3D tennis court fills the viewport under a deep green wash. A two-line title is left-aligned 12.5% in from the left and sits just below centre: line one the brand name in a cream high-contrast serif, line two the game name in yellow wide grotesk at about 9.7vw, reaching 80% of the width. A tiny paddle-and-ball graphic fills the gap after line one. A hairline spans 75% of the width beneath; under it an outlined pill sits at the left end and a filled yellow pill with a ball icon at the right, with tiny uppercase legal text below. Logo top-left, hamburger top-right.
type: Digest reports MonaSans throughout, weight 400, uppercase, zero tracking; the game name is 140px in a slightly wide cut. The brand line is drawn as a high-contrast serif wordmark at the same cap height. Three sizes only: title, 28–44px button labels, 11px legal.
colour: #092617 #122815 #f4cf4e #efeadb #00503c — Everything lives inside one bottle-green field; cream for the brand line and outlines, a single warm yellow for the game name and primary button. No section changes.
imagery: A real-time 3D tennis court with branded hoardings, pushed far back by a dark green overlay and fine grain so it reads as texture; a flat vector paddle and ball are the only bright objects.
layout: One screen, no scroll. The content block is inset 12.5% each side and stacked in three bands: title, hairline, action row, with buttons pushed to opposite ends of the rule. On mobile the primary button is bracketed between two rules and right-aligned.

sections.description: The action row is the only other element: a hairline with slightly wobbly, hand-drawn edges, then two pills on one baseline at opposite ends. The secondary is a 2px cream outline about 255×95px with a pale label; the primary is a solid yellow capsule about 340×95px with a dark ball icon and dark label near 44px. Legal copy hangs under the secondary button, left-aligned, in bold 12px uppercase at reduced opacity.

steal: Drop a small object from the product (here the game's paddle and ball) into the empty space at the end of a short headline line so the lockup itself carries the concept.
Set a two-line title with line one in a serif wordmark and line two in a wide grotesk at the same cap height, separated by colour rather than size.
Use a full 3D scene as wallpaper by burying it under a roughly 85–90% tint of the brand colour, so it adds depth without competing with type.
media: A real-time 3D tennis stadium covers the whole first screen, dimmed under a deep-green wash to near texture so the type carries the screen; the only foreground picture is a small flat pictogram of the game tucked beside the wordmark. No photographs and no video.
motion: The loader runs at least 4.5s as a looping preview of the game: a ball drops on a gravity ease (0.5s cubic-bezier(.5,.05,1,.5)) onto a paddle sliding on a 3s loop. The title screen then arrives in a stagger, wordmark first, each part fading and rising over 0.8s cubic-bezier(.215,.61,.355,1), after which wheel steps do nothing and only the WebGL camera drifts round the stadium; the house ease is cubic-bezier(.55,0,.1,1), 51 uses, at .3s and .5s.

name: The Tie-break
idea: The start screen of a branded tennis game, where the lines of a court seen from above become the frame around the title; only this screen was captured.
hero: A heavily blurred, grainy photograph of a figure in a cream jacket on a blue court fills the viewport. Thin white-to-blue lines trace a tennis court in plan across the whole screen: two horizontals near the top, two near the bottom, an inner rectangle about 45% of the viewport wide, and centre ticks; every line stops short of the middle column to leave it clear. In that column, stacked and centred: two partner logos, a two-line italic serif title at 112px (7.8vw) broken at its hyphen, three lines of 12px sans, and a small white button with a ball icon inside a hairline outer frame.
type: Instrument Serif italic at 112px for the title, white, sentence case with an exclamation mark; Work Sans 12px for the description and button label. Only two sizes, roughly a 9x jump, plus the stacked co-brand logos.
colour: #335483 #284879 #d8ccbc #1e3a8c #ffffff #8a3b45 — Cool court blues dominate, with the blurred cream jacket as a warm mass behind the title and a hint of red at the lower edge; type, lines and button are white.
imagery: One campaign photograph blurred until it is only colour masses and overlaid with coarse noise, used full-bleed as a field. On mobile the crop turns grey and darker with heavier grain.
layout: Single screen. A centre column about 22% of the viewport wide holds all content; the rest is the blurred field ruled by court lines that run to every edge. No navigation, no footer.
steal: Draw the subject's own geometry, here court lines in plan, as hairlines across the full viewport and interrupt them where content sits.
Blur a campaign photo until it is only colour masses, add coarse grain, and use it as the background so white type stays readable.
Frame a small solid button with a second hairline outline a few pixels outside it.
media: One fixed WebGL canvas covers the whole first screen with a product close-up blurred until only colour masses remain (pale grey felt, denim blue corners, a red stripe), under a radial warp and grain; text covers about 7.5% (16.9% on the phone). A line diagram of a tennis court is drawn over it as the layout frame; no video and no content images, the canvas drifting slowly like ambient footage.
motion: The preloader is up through all four intro frames: an outline ball bouncing with squash (scale 1.3 by 0.65) and a growing shadow on a 0.8s loop, falling on an ease-in and rising on an ease-out. The title screen then fades in, heading, paragraph and button each on a 2s ease opacity, and the page never scrolls: views switch on a fast 0.17s fade, and the button border changes over 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.19,1,0.22,1).

name: Lenny’s Newsletter Product Pass
idea: A perks membership presented as a conference lanyard badge, with every partner offer drawn as a tear-off coupon ticket.
hero: Peach field. A floating pill navigation bar about 72% of the viewport wide sits 40px from the top: script wordmark with campfire mascot at left, three links and an orange outlined pill button at right. Below, a two-column split. The left 45% holds a three-line bold sans headline at about 2.8vw, a three-line paragraph, then a wide white email pill with thick black outline and an orange arrow button inside its right end. On the right, two illustrated badge cards hang on orange lanyard straps that run off the top edge behind the nav, tilted against each other. A tan logo marquee runs edge to edge along the bottom.
type: Degular in bold for headings and regular for body, sentence case, no tracking; hero headline about 40px against 20px body, section titles 64px and centred. A brush-script wordmark and a hand-lettered marker face (faveHandPro) on each coupon's value label supply the personality.
colour: #fff1e8 #fdd4b5 #ffffff #f6871f #111111 #d9a67e — Everything lives in one orange family: pale peach page, deeper peach panels, saturated orange only on buttons and lanyards, black outlines for structure. Partner logos keep their own colours inside white cards.
imagery: Flat vector illustration with thick black outlines: lanyard badges, campfire mascot, yellow starburst stickers. Otherwise third-party logos, tan-tinted in the marquee and full colour inside cards. No photography.
layout: The hero is a left-anchored split; everything after is a centred heading over a three-column grid of identical coupon cards repeated for about seven screens, the first group wrapped in a wide rounded peach panel. The closing panel returns to a split.

sections.description: Three-column grid of coupon cards, white with a 2px black outline and 14px radius. Each card stacks: partner logo top-left, one bold line stating the offer, two or three lines of grey description, then a dotted perforation line and a peach stub with a hand-lettered dollar value at left and a small claim link at right. Some cards carry a yellow starburst sticker rotated over the top-right corner, breaking the outline.

A wide peach panel with black outline and large radius, inset from the page edges. Left half: two-line bold heading, short paragraph, orange outlined pill button. Right half: a single column of partner logos stacked vertically and clipped by the panel's top and bottom edges, reading as a vertical ticker. Below the panel the footer is one row: script wordmark left, four links and the pill button right.

steal: Draw each offer as a physical coupon with a dotted perforation line, a tinted stub and a hand-lettered value, so a long grid of logos reads as tickets instead of cards.
Hang the hero illustration from the top edge of the viewport and pass it behind the floating nav so the page seems to continue above the screen.
Tint all partner logos in one brand-derived tan for the marquee and save their full colour for the cards where they matter.

name: Heron AI
idea: An AI agent that checks architects' models for code problems, shown as a drafting sheet: elevations and floor plans on warm paper, where the product's job is acted out with flat orange flags on the drawings instead of being described with abstract tech imagery.
hero: Warm drafting paper inside a 7px inset frame. Between two full-width rules at y≈78 and y≈748, one contained drawing box (about 95% of the width and 72% of the height) holds a stippled, hatched concrete house elevation about 960px wide with bare trees, standing on a drawn ground line, with two tiny flat-orange squares on the facade as hotspots. Nothing else shows in the captured fold: the two-line 47px (3.2vw) uppercase bold title is docked under the lower rule at y≈775 and reveals only after the first scroll, beside a 13px intro box and an orange link. Before that a 4.5s loader draws the house as line art stroke by stroke while a spec table fills in bottom-right.
type: BT Grotesk (73% of text, 400-700) for everything readable: titles in uppercase at 47, 40 and 23px (3.2, 2.8 and 1.6vw), leading 1.0, -0.02em; body at 12-13px. Geist Mono 500 (27%) at 10-12px uppercase for labels, bracketed indices and prompts. No serif and no italic. The house version keeps the grotesk alone, in sentence case, with 16px body.
colour: #f4f3ec #282828 #626260 #b4b4b0 #fa3600 — Warm drafting paper as the ground for almost the whole page; ink for 86% of the text and for dark fills (plan walls, tab headers); a pale grey for words not yet read; one flat orange at about 2-3% of the surface for a sun disc, the violation flags, link text and approve buttons. White appears only as text on ink or orange.
imagery: Strictly monochrome architectural drawings in two registers, pure line art and dense stippled etching with hatched shadows, plus floor plans, isometric line icons and a product interface fragment set in the same paper tones. Colour enters only as flat orange shapes, never as tinted photography. Square corners, no shadows, paper grain underneath.
layout: Text starts 26px inside a 7px inset frame, at x=33. Every section spans the full frame and is cut into cells by 1px rules: halves, four columns of about 357px, two thirds plus a one-third copy rail. Sections butt against each other with no vertical gaps. An 8-viewport sticky stage carries the main story, and a zigzag of looping 464px vignettes leaves half of some screens as bare grid paper. The house version keeps the cells and marks them with tone steps and space instead of rules.

sections.description: Split at the centre. Left half: a tower drawn as line art merging into an etched render through a stepped pixel mask, a large flat orange disc behind its top. Right half: an uppercase statement of about 33px over eight lines, about 440px wide, that fills from grey to ink as you scroll, with an outlined button below.

Four columns of about 357px under a header row (a two-line 40px heading left, a short paragraph right). Each column holds an isometric line icon that draws itself on (a slab pierced by a cylinder, a cube inside a circle), a 23px uppercase title in three short lines and 13px grey body.

A sticky full-frame stage held for about 8 viewports. A floor plan about 520x640 builds in layers: heavy ink walls, then fine furniture and stairs, then dimension strings, then three orange squares flagging the problems, one with an arrow. A caption card about 230px wide, docked 33px from the bottom-left, changes its text at each beat. The plan then slides into the left two thirds for a one-third copy rail of four short claims.

A product interface fragment in the middle cell, about 5/12 of the width: four figure tiles, an activity list, and an overlapping approval panel with flat orange buttons, all in the page's paper tones, with a chat panel on a plan fragment above it.

steal: Draw the pictures in the product's own medium: for a tool that works on architectural models, plans and elevations that build in stages (structure, then detail, then dimensions, then the flagged problems) instead of abstract 3D or glowing shapes.
Reveal a picture by a stepped pixel dissolve from line art to shaded render, about 19 steps in 0.58s, so the motif itself shows a line becoming a model.

Spend one flat accent on about 2-3% of the surface and only on what demands attention (the problem flags, one disc, the primary action) on a warm paper ground with near-black ink. The site separates everything with 1px rules, monospace labels and bracketed indices, all banned here: keep the cells, mark them with tone steps and space, and set labels in the text face.
media: Every picture is a drawing, never a photograph or a video: one contained etched elevation centred on paper (box about 95% wide and 72% high), a drawing held in one half against a statement, a sticky full-frame plan that builds beside a docked caption card, and 464px looping vignettes in a zigzag. Twenty-seven images, nine inline SVG drawings and paper-grain backgrounds.
motion: A 4.5s loader draws the house stroke by stroke, then a stepped pixel dissolve (mask position over 0.58s in 19 steps) swaps line art for etching. Lenis and 52 ScrollTriggers run the rest: lines rise with opacity and yPercent over 0.8-1.08s power2.out at a 0.02 stagger, the big statement fills grey to ink on a scrub, the plan builds in layers inside an 8074px CSS-sticky wrap, vignettes loop on a 5s linear cycle with their own eases, and hovers move over 0.48s cubic-bezier(0.625,0.05,0,1).

name: Huy Phan
idea: The whole portfolio is one fixed viewing stage: nineteen projects hang on a 3D helix that the wheel turns, each landing flat in the centre, while a giant counter, a wheel of project names and a credit block swap around it like readouts on an instrument panel.
hero: A single fixed 1440x900 stage on light grey (#ececec) with 20px margins and a 16-column grid. The active project picture lies flat in the centre, about 380x300 (26% of the width), tilted about 1 degree; earlier cards spiral up and off the top edge, and the next ones fan down-left in perspective behind a 180px (12.5vw) index number with a small total beside it, bottom-left. Left third: a 55px vertical wordmark strip, a four-item uppercase nav at 19px and credit pairs (role, launch month, recognition). Right: a wheel of all project names centred at x≈1150, the active one dark and its neighbours faded, with three 12px colour swatches at the far edge. No headline and no readable name or role on the stage; before it a 5s intro shows a line-drawn mascot pushing a black curtain off a red two-line wordmark.
type: Three families. A neutral grotesk carries 95% of the characters: medium at 10px for labels, credits and descriptions, regular at 180px for the index number (leading 0.85, -0.04em; 90px on the phone). A narrow glyphic display face with flared terminals sets the nav (19px), project names (16px caps) and panel headings (23px), tracking +0.01em. A contrasty display face is kept for the red intro wordmark. The house version is one family with 16px descriptions.
colour: #ececec #1e1e1e #c4c4c4 #d4d4d4 #171717 #ff4949 — Light grey ground on 85-90% of the screen with near-black ink and faded grey list text; red only for the intro wordmark. All other colour comes from the photographs and three swatches per project. Much of the readout is white in difference blend so it inverts over the moving cards.
imagery: Nineteen screenshots and stills of client websites in one landscape ratio of about 5:4, square corners, each keeping its own grading (neon blue to pastel); the cards bend like paper with scroll speed and lie flat at rest. A line-drawn mascot, and an illustrated self-portrait that alternates with the vertical wordmark.
layout: One 900px screen; scrollY stays 0. Three zones balance across the width: labels and credits in the left third anchored at x=197 (column 3) and x=287 (column 4), the picture in the middle, the name wheel in columns 12 to 15. Empty space runs in a diagonal round the active card and the helix sweeps through it, so it reads as placed. On the phone everything collapses into one centred column with the image at 60% of the width.

sections.description: A white field with a black panel over the right 70%. A small line-drawn character, about 15% of the viewport tall, pushes the panel right over about 2.5s to uncover a two-line red wordmark, centred; then the project cards sweep in as a steep diagonal cascade from top-right to bottom-left, bent like pages, and settle into the helix.

The right-hand wheel of all project names in 16px display caps, each with a 10px category above, a short dash and a three-line 10px description; only the active item is dark, and neighbours fade to about 20% contrast towards the top and bottom of the right 40% of the screen.
The left credit block: label and value pairs for role, launch month and a recognition list of one to six lines, labels grey and values near-black, swapping with a short blur and fade on every step.

steal: Change the content, not the layout: one fixed stage where only the active picture, its name and its credits swap per step. The site lets a 180px index number carry the hierarchy; the house rules ban index numbering, so set the project name that large instead.
Let 3D cards bend with scroll speed and lie flat at rest, so the active picture is always a clean, undistorted rectangle of about a quarter of the width.

Anchor a sparse three-zone screen to one grid (labels in one column, values in the next, the picture centred, the list on the right) so a fixed stage reads as composed, and swap text in under half a second (opacity about 0.3s ease) so the visitor never waits for words.
media: One fixed WebGL canvas covers the screen, but pictures fill about 30% of it: the active card is about 9% of the area, and the rest is the helix of neighbours cut by the top edge and the bottom-left corner. No video on the stage; a showreel sits behind a link.
motion: A 5s intro, in which a mascot pushes a curtain aside and the cards cascade in bent like pages, follows a 9.2s load. Each wheel notch then jumps six projects round an endless loop of nineteen, the cards bending with velocity and the counter and credits crossfading through a blur (opacity 0.32s ease on 270 elements, background-color 0.52s cubic-bezier(0.22,0.61,0.36,1)), with no split text and no reduced-motion rule.

name: Ciao Energy
idea: The can is the whole website: one fixed real-time 3D studio scene in which the camera travels from a flavour carousel to extreme close-ups of the can's own label, where each claim is paired with the ingredient that was taken out, and the copy is a thin layer over the product.
hero: A fixed full-viewport 3D canvas on a dark grey studio floor fading to black over the top 40%. A metallic can stands dead centre (about 16% of the width, half the height), tilted about 10 degrees, between a chrome ring hovering above and a dark plinth below; six darker, smaller cans recede on a shallow arc behind it, the outer two cut by the viewport edges. The flavour name sits on the plinth in two lines of heavy italic uppercase at about 36px, over a 480px slider and a small scroll prompt; thin chevrons about 140px either side of the can change flavour. A centred logo about 125px wide at the top, a sound toggle left, a white contact pill right. No headline: the benefits arrive one scroll later.
type: Three families. A heavy (900) italic uppercase grotesque with leading 0.8 for headings only: about 45px for feature headings, 108px (7.5vw) for the FAQ, about 190px cap height for the slogan. A neutral geometric grotesque at 16px, leading about 1.6, for body, and 18px weight 500 for FAQ questions. A monospace at 11-12px uppercase for tags, the prompt and the nav; the house version keeps those labels in the text face, sentence case, at 16px.
colour: #000000 #6a6a6a #ffffff #3d2b68 #9a8ae6 — Black page (about 60% of pixels) and a grey studio floor fading to black; all text and buttons white. One custom property carries the flavour colour (a deep violet here) and tints the close-ups and the light, and a lilac accent marks the active claim. Every other colour comes from the cans themselves. The site's blue-to-pink slider is a gradient; the house version is a flat bar in the flavour colour.
imagery: No photographs or video: one art-directed render set of about twelve aluminium cans in six flavours, a chrome ring and a plinth, under soft key lights, with depth falloff on the background cans and a flavour-tinted spot and haze on the close-ups. Always full-bleed, never boxed or rounded.
layout: Two insets: the interface at 4% (58px) for the menu, the sound toggle and a progress bar; the content at 10% (x=144), a copy column about 400px wide and vertically centred, leaving the centre-right 40-50% to the product. Eight beats of 1.25 viewports each (about 14 screens) are empty scroll spacers that move the camera; the DOM layout barely changes. After the footer the scroll loops back to the carousel.

sections.description: Pinned label close-ups. The camera comes so close that one can fills a tilted band about 450px wide, cropped by the top or bottom edge, its printed label repeating the claim. Left at x=144, about 400px wide: a small tag naming the removed ingredient, a two-line heavy italic heading at about 45px, three lines of 16px body. A rail of four round 50px buttons at the right margin shows the active claim. Each beat re-angles the camera.
A two-word slogan in heavy italic uppercase across about 80% of the width at about 40% white, cap height near 190px, on a blurred lilac wash, with the can floating in front of the middle letters.
The whole range with no text: twelve cans in every flavour colour lined up on a sweeping diagonal from lower left to upper right, bleeding off both edges over the grey studio floor.

A 108px heavy italic heading at x=144, then a 670px accordion offset right of centre: 18px questions in rows about 64px tall, each with a small chevron. A centred newsletter block about 490px wide closes the page.

steal: For a single physical product, keep one fixed full-viewport render and move the camera, never the layout: beats of about 1.25 viewports, each with its own angle, plus real DOM text so a slow GPU or a failed WebGL context still shows every claim.
Pair each claim with an extreme close-up of the product's own printed label in a tilted band beside a 400px copy column set 10% from the left, so the object proves the sentence next to it.

Bind the accent to the product variant with one custom property that changes over 0.6s when the flavour changes, and let the scene's light follow it. The site floats the can over its slogan; under the house rules nothing covers a statement, so set the object beside or below the type.
media: One fixed WebGL canvas covers 100% of every screen and holds the only pictures: product renders, no photographs and no video. The product stands centre in the hero, then fills a tilted band beside the copy column, then sweeps the whole range diagonally across the frame.
motion: Fourteen ScrollTriggers on empty 1125px spacers set about 26 scene values (camera, can spin, arc spacing, light, tint) that short 0.09-0.12s power1.inOut tweens chase, so the camera moves continuously between beats. Headings, split into 382 characters, enter with opacity, scale and y over 0.6s power2.out and leave over 0.9s power2.in with a 0.25s stagger; the flavour colour eases over 0.6s, and the full scene took 12.7s to load.

name: Neutomni
idea: A small web studio sells its websites like packaged goods, printed in one red ink on white paper: the preloader is a cut-along-the-line coupon, the prices are tear-off tickets with barcodes, and the process is a square wheel that rounds off as the bumpy road from A to B smooths out.
hero: White page with 20px margins. A full-width red wordmark 1400x230 (97% of the width, 26% of the height) runs across the top; 10px under it a 13px row holds a one-line descriptor at the left, the nav from the centre line at x=720 and an italic email flush right. The 52px headline sits in the right half from x=720, two upright sans lines and a closing line in italic serif. A dark 576x360 video card of case-study screens is centred at the bottom and cropped by the fold, about 230px showing. Small local time and a pulsing open-for-work dot sit in the bottom corners. No button.
type: Three voices. A neutral grotesque at 400 (61% of characters) for headings and 16px body at 1.2 leading; an italic high-contrast serif (19%) that always takes the closing clause of a headline; a monospace (19%) for 13px uppercase labels, the process equation and price lines. Fixed steps of 118px (8.2vw), 80, 60, 52 and 32px, no clamp(), nothing bold, leading 1.0 for the sans and 0.9 for the italic. The house rules ban the italic accent clause and the monospace: one face per headline, labels in the text face.
colour: #cf1830 #ffffff #1a1a1a #6db1f0 #f8f4f4 — One ink: red for 63% of all text (5.5:1 on white) and for a few full grounds (preloader, process columns, footer, one price card) on a white page. A near-black band for the reel, and one sky blue saved for the pricing scene, where the site floods it in as a rising glow; the house version cuts to a flat sky field.
imagery: Staged mockup photographs of the studio's sites on real devices in real scenes (a monitor in a hedge, a tablet in robot arms, a phone on a desk) in soft daylight, square corners; a small founders photo; a 38s looping reel of case-study screens; white line drawing for the process. Only the price tickets get rounded corners and soft shadows.
layout: 20px margins, and the page is built on its centre line: the nav, the hero headline, the founders photo and the counter-statements all start at x=720 while the left half holds small metadata or the opposite statement. Sections butt against each other with no conventional padding; runways of about 3448px (process), 2288px (work) and 7080px (pricing) carry the pinned scenes, so 450 words fill about 24 screens.

sections.description: Split on the centre line: a 60px four-line statement from x=20 in the left half, and a small founders photograph 340x165 dropped at x=720 beside it.

Pinned for about 4 viewports on a 1400x900 stage: four red columns about 340px wide with 12px gaps rise from the bottom as a stepped bar chart until all reach about 720px. One white drawing runs across all four: a dashed guide at about 30% of the height, a wavy road below it that flattens column by column, and an outline shape that rolls along the guide and turns from square to circle. Each column ends in a 20px title and a three-line description in white.

A sticky split: a two-line 118px section title at the top left and a three-row project index at the bottom left (32px italic names, the active row in full red, the others faded), facing a staged device photograph that takes 60-65% of the width and the full height, bleeding off the right edge and wiping in with a clip-path for each project.

A sky-blue field rises from the bottom until it floods the screen; an 80px centred white headline blurs its upright lines while the closing line stays sharp, and three ticket cards fly up tilted in 3D perspective, two white receipts with a perforated edge and a barcode and one red card.

steal: Print with one ink: every word in a single saturated colour on a white ground, with a second hue kept for one late scene so it lands as an event, not a theme.

Tell a process with one drawing that crosses all the step blocks (a shape turning from square to circle while the road under it flattens) inside a pinned stage of 3-4 viewports, and keep the blocks as plain colour with a short title and three lines of copy.

Turn pricing into objects you could tear off and keep: ticket cards with a perforated edge and a drawn barcode, tilted 5-15 degrees in perspective. Under the house rules they carry no resting shadow and the price is set in the text face, not monospace.
media: Media covers about 35% of the first screen: the full-width wordmark across the top and a video card peeking from the fold, which grows into a sticky full-screen dark reel. Later pictures are a small photograph on the centre line, staged device photographs filling 60-65% of the width in a sticky split, and a canvas stage of rising red columns; one 38s looping video with no poster.
motion: A 3.5s red preloader in which scissors travel along a dotted cut line, the wordmark already in its final place. Under Lenis, lines blur and rise in at 'top 85%' over 0.52-0.64s power1.out with a 0.12s stagger, the process shape morphs over 1s power2.inOut, the work pin scrubs at 0.8 with 0.9s power2.inOut clip-path wipes and inactive rows at 0.28 opacity, and the pricing runway runs about 7000px with no reduced-motion rule.

name: Belgrade Arbor
idea: A residential and office complex whose facade branches like a tree canopy, and every device on the site follows from that one image: photographs cut into rounded branch-like shards, forest-green and vanilla grounds, bronze titles and one sprout-lime accent.
hero: Built as a full-bleed 1440x900 video scrubbed by scroll under a fixed WebGL canvas, with no poster; in the capture neither painted, so the desktop first screen stayed plain vanilla (#fdfbef) for the whole 4.5s with only a centred dark pill nav about 640x58 at y≈24 (menu left, a small gold tree mark centre, an outlined enquiry pill right). On the phone the fold is a grey pencil drawing of the branch-columned facade filling the screen and fading to white at the bottom, where a 66px name is lost in the wash. The real message, that the facade follows a tree canopy, first appears one screen down as a six-line 56px serif paragraph.
type: Two families. A light old-style editorial serif (300 roman and italic, 400) carries every statement and every list at 56px (3.9vw), leading 1.1, tracking +0.02em; uppercase chapter titles run at about 10.5vw and 13vw with leading near 0.9, and one letter-spaced word reaches about 17vw. Work Sans 400/500 does body at 16px, small paragraphs at 14px, and the tracked uppercase labels and buttons. Active list items turn italic.
colour: #fdfbef #2e3a26 #a68150 #ccbf99 #fff4d6 #e7fd55 #314759 — Vanilla page with pine-green text and dark grounds; bronze for serif titles on light, sand for caps on dark, cream for text on green. An acid lime covers about 2% of the page (labels, the active tab, links), and one late chapter turns slate blue. The pinned chapter sits on a moss-green gradient, which the house version makes a flat moss field.
imagery: Warm, soft architectural renders and photographs (sunlit marble, linen, a stair with a tree, dining and lounge interiors) masked into rounded irregular polygons that echo the canopy, and full-bleed macros of folded cream cloth and teal woven upholstery used as grounds for titles. A line-drawn isometric street map with bronze pins, an aerial render on a small rounded card, and a portrait clip of a man crossing a marble lobby.
layout: 64px side gutters. Every section is exactly one viewport tall and the chapters meet edge to edge, each marked by a change of ground (vanilla, moss, full-bleed photograph, vanilla, slate) rather than padding. Most screens are half splits, text 64-690 against media on the right, then mirrored. A 9-viewport sticky stage opens the page, and a floating pill nav sits over the top of each section, where it collides with labels and body text.

sections.description: Pinned for 8100px on moss green. Left column at x=64, about 625px wide: a small lime label, a 56px light serif paragraph of five or six lines, and an outlined pill to explore the building in 3D. Right half: two rounded shard-shaped photo masks, a large one about 410x550 and a small one about 225x285 overlapping its lower-left corner and set about 60px lower; the pictures crossfade inside the same shapes. The next paragraph swaps sides. A 280px progress bar with a counter sits bottom-left.
Same green ground: a two-line uppercase serif headline at about 10.5vw running almost margin to margin, then a 14px paragraph about 320px wide offset to x≈830 below it, and an underlined lime link.

Split. Left, x=64-610: six nearby places stacked as 56px light bronze serif lines about 30px apart. Right 60%: a line-drawn isometric street map with bronze pins and the building as a small gold block with a flag.

An opener of folded cream cloth, full-bleed below a 176px vanilla strip, with one bronze uppercase serif word at about 13vw docked bottom-left 150px above the fold. The next screen splits 50/50: unit types as 56px pine serif links on an 80px pitch, the active one in italic, facing a slider of eleven portrait interior renders with round arrows at mid-height.

steal: Take one shape from the subject's own form and use it as the picture mask throughout: here canopy-like rounded polygons, a large and a small one overlapping opposite the text column, swapping sides with each paragraph.

Make lists the headlines: places, unit types and wings set as 56px light serif lines on an 80px pitch, the active one in the accent colour, each list facing a picture, a map or a slider in the other half.

Give every section exactly one viewport and change the ground colour or the full-bleed picture at each, so the scroll reads as chapters without padding bands; open a chapter with a full-bleed close-up of a material and one uppercase word at about 13vw docked bottom-left, coloured from a tone in that material.
media: Pictures carry most screens: the pinned chapter pairs two shard-masked photographs opposite the text, chapter openers are full-bleed material close-ups and looping footage, and later chapters split 50/50 between a serif list and a map, a portrait slider or a portrait clip. Six muted videos, none autoplaying; the 16s hero clip has no poster and never painted on desktop.
motion: Lenis drives a 9-viewport sticky stage where the ground turns from vanilla to moss, serif paragraphs blur and rise in word by word (939 split characters) and photographs crossfade inside the shards; caps titles sharpen character by character, and one giant word widens its letter spacing with the scroll. The only observed CSS transition is opacity 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); the rest is script-driven (.65s the commonest stylesheet duration), and the page took 12.2s to load.

name: Nick Ho
idea: A young racing driver's sponsor pitch built from the paddock's own objects: the car number as the hero, the helmet as the sponsor wall, the season calendar as a track the car drives down, a gallery dial that reads like a rev counter and a chequered-flag hand-off, all in black, white and greyscale photography with one signal yellow for what is live.
hero: A full-bleed greyscale photograph of the driver in his helmet beside the car fills the screen as a WebGL depth-map canvas, with a 288px dark scrim at the bottom. Dead centre, the car number in white condensed figures at about 216px (15vw) dominates. Three stacked stats (figure plus 14px label) at the left, a right-aligned column of short facts at the right edge; the name as the h1 bottom-left in condensed caps at only 50px (3.5vw) over a three-line 14px intro, and the next race bottom-right. No visible nav or action: only a 24px yellow square menu button top-right and a small monogram top-left.
type: An Anton-style condensed display grotesk, uppercase, 400-600, tracking 0, leading 1.0-1.1, for every heading, figure, button label and event name: one heading size of 50px (3.5vw), event names at about 26px, the hero number at 15vw. System Helvetica 400/700 for body at 13-14px. The house version keeps the condensed face and the single heading size and raises body to 16px.
colour: #000000 #ffffff #fed60a #333333 #f0f0f0 — Black (43% of grounds) and white (53%) alternating every one or two screens with hard cuts; #333 for heading text on white; one signal yellow on about 8% of grounds and 3% of text, used only for state: the menu button, buttons, the active calendar row, two highlighted phrases and the gauge needle.
imagery: Motorsport photography of the driver, car, track and paddock, all filtered to greyscale and given colour back only when active or hovered; cut-out pictures of the helmet and a top-down car used as objects on flat ground; a 22s muted on-track clip. Square corners almost everywhere; ratios of 5:4, 0.83 portrait, 4:3, 1:1 and 16:10 by section.
layout: 80px side margins on every text section and a 7-column grid of about 206px, drawn as faint vertical guides across the hero and the white sections (the house version keeps the grid and drops the guides). Sticky runs hold the helmet wall, the about chapters and the calendar; a carousel bleeds off the right edge on purpose. Breathing room comes from whole-screen colour fields rather than padding, though about 250px of white after the statement and a 1712px mostly empty logo run are real holes.

sections.description: A cut-out photograph of the race helmet about 380px wide held sticky in the centre and turning to a new angle between steps, while monochrome partner logos stream past in four staggered columns at different speeds; a small yellow partner button arrives under the helmet at the end.

Sticky on black in three zones: the chapter title at x=80 in 50px condensed caps, a vertical strip of 302x362 portrait photographs at x=515 spaced every 404px (the active one in colour, its neighbours greyscale and peeking at the edges), and a 410px paragraph at the right; five chapters over about 2500px, with a chapter count and a yellow skip button.

The season calendar: full-width rows about 83px tall on black, the event name in 26px condensed caps, a 14px series line and the date right-aligned. A top-down cut-out of the car (320x573) parks between the words of the heading, then drives down the centre of the list as you scroll; the current event's row turns yellow.

A dial carousel: square photographs on the arc of a 1756px circle, the active one upright and in colour at the top centre, the others greyscale and turned along the curve, over a tick gauge with a yellow needle like a rev counter.

steal: Turn the subject's own objects into navigation: a vehicle sliding down a schedule as the you-are-here marker, a carousel shaped like a gauge, flag tiles as the one soft transition. Each carries information as well as character.
Filter every photograph to greyscale and give colour back only to the active or hovered item (filter about 0.4s), so 28 mixed photographs read as one set and colour itself means 'current'.

Use one signal colour for state only, about 8% of grounds and 3% of text, on a black-and-white page that alternates every one or two screens with hard cuts, and let exactly one glyph that belongs to the subject (here the car number) jump to 15vw against a single 50px heading size, with the name as the h1 beside it.
media: A greyscale depth-map photograph covers 100% of the first screen. Later pictures are a sticky cut-out helmet among streaming logos, a vertical portrait strip, a carousel bleeding off the right edge, a cut-out car that travels down the calendar, an inset clip that grows to full bleed, and a dial of square photographs: 28 images, one 22s muted clip, one WebGL canvas.
motion: There is no entrance (the page took 12.3s to load), and Lenis runs 97 ScrollTriggers with no pins: CSS sticky holds the helmet, the chapters and the calendar, 19 yPercent scrubs move the logo columns and stretched background words, and the video frame grows from an inset with about 54px margins to full bleed by scrubbing width, height and corner radius. Photographs regain colour over 0.4s, menu items slide over 0.5s cubic-bezier(.7,0,.3,1), button labels roll per character at a 0.018s stagger, and content blanks out mid-scroll under the smooth-scroll lag.

name: Odyssée
idea: A medical-aesthetics clinic presented like a skincare editorial: soft-lit close-ups of skin and slow muted loops carry the page, a thin navy serif voice argues for method over myth, and the page ends on a rolling pearl engraved with the wordmark, one polished object that stands for the result.
hero: A full-bleed muted video portrait (a woman resting her chin on her hands in pale grey-blue studio light) fills the screen, followed at once by a second full-bleed close-up of lips and jaw. No headline: a single 42px strip crosses the exact vertical middle in white, the serif wordmark at x=20, an 18px serif tagline about medical aesthetics at column 3 (x≈255), and four tiny tracked caps links on the right ending in the booking link, which all but vanishes against the pale picture. The strip holds while both pictures pass under it, then becomes a sticky 42px header. The entrance is a flat warm grey veil carrying only the wordmark and tagline, lifting over about 2.5s.
type: Two families. psTimes, a condensed Times-style serif at weight 350, for statements at 48px (3.3vw) and 32px and for titles and the tagline at 18px, sentence case, leading about 1.0-1.05, every statement with a first-line indent of one column. Basel Grotesk at 430 for 14px body and 12px lightly tracked uppercase labels and links; the house version sets those in sentence case at 16px. Fixed px sizes per breakpoint, no clamp().
colour: #fffcf8 #1e305e #ffffff #28292a — A warm cream ground behind nearly everything, one deep navy for 88% of the text, the progress rule and a duotone on secondary pictures, white only over photographs. A single small red dot on a live clock is the only accent; the photographs supply skin tones, pale grey-blue studio grounds and a champagne pearl.
imagery: Soft, even studio light on pale grey-blue backgrounds, natural skin with no retouching gloss, tight crops (lips, eye, nostril, knees) and one face turned 90 degrees for tension; slow, nearly still muted loops of skin, serum drops and bubbles used as living photographs; a navy duotone on two link cards. Square corners and cover crops everywhere.
layout: 20px outer margins on a 12-column grid (columns about 117px). Text has two anchors: column 3 (x≈255) for statements, body and labels, and the exact centre line for right-half paragraphs and cards. Media is always full-bleed, an exact half (720/720) or flush tiles with no gutter. Cream gaps of 232-552px separate sections, roughly one idea per screen; the closing contacts huddle in the left half.

sections.description: A 48px light serif statement on three lines from column 3 to the right margin with a one-column first-line indent, a small 108x161 double-portrait thumbnail docked at the left margin, then 14px body in a narrow column and a booking link.

Pinned for four steps: a counter, a label and a 1400px rule whose navy fill grows a quarter per step, over four 350x263 muted 5s video tiles flush edge to edge; the active tile at full strength, the other three washed to about 10%, each with an 18px serif title beneath.

Split on the centre line: a tall 672x1233 muted skin close-up holds the right half while scrolling, a small 233x291 clip of a serum drop sits just left of centre with a short caption, and a three-word 48px serif headline arrives at x=20 at mid-height.

Contact rows, an opening-hours table where only today is in full navy, and a live local clock with a pulsing dot; then the page lifts away to reveal a fixed full-bleed 9s loop of a pearl rolling on a pale grey surface with the wordmark engraved round it.

steal: Make video behave like photographs: muted, looping, with posters, 5-29s of nearly still subjects started by script when they come into view, square corners and cover crops everywhere.

Give every serif statement a first-line indent of exactly one grid column and anchor the block at column 3 with 20px outer margins, so the indent reads as a deliberate grid step; use the exact centre line as the second anchor for half-width pictures and right-half paragraphs.

End on real local detail (an hours table that marks today, a live local clock), then reveal a fixed full-bleed brand object as the last screen. The site's tiny white caps nav over pale skin all but disappears; the house version is a plain bar with the booking action as a real button.
media: Video is the main medium: a 27s portrait loop and a second close-up fill the first screen, then four 5s tiles flush edge to edge, a 720/720 diptych, a tall half-width clip held while scrolling, a full-bleed band that fades up from cream, two navy duotone cards, and a fixed pearl loop revealed under the footer. Nine images and eight muted, looping videos with posters, started by script; no canvas.
motion: No preloader: a warm grey veil lifts off the hero video over about 2.5-3s with the type already in place. Under Lenis the features section pins for four steps, cross-fading tiles over 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) as the navy rule grows, images fade over 0.5s cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1), underlines grow by background-size over .4s expo-out and the page lifts off a fixed bottom layer to reveal the pearl, but content is opacity-gated, so mid-scroll frames show empty cream, and there is no reduced-motion rule.

name: USAvionix
idea: A maker of autonomous jet drones explains its product as a single mission played out on scroll: one pinned WebGL camera flies from a lone drone over forested mountains to a swarm, to detection overlays and then to a dark tactical map, while a console readout runs at the edges and three status colours (observed, threat, secured) carry the plot.
hero: After a preloader that shows only the dimmed drone silhouette for over 4.5s, a full-bleed real-time scene: photoreal forested mountains seen from above with a matte black flying wing dead centre, wingspan about 560px (39% of the width). A three-line claim at 80px (5.6vw), Geist 600, -0.04em, leading 0.95, sits top-left at x=32, y 88-300; a three-line 29px lead is docked bottom-right (x 874-1384) over a translucent grey pill about 248x40 that prompts the scroll. A grey contact pill and a menu button are fixed top-right, and a one-word chapter code with sliding tick rails sits top-centre. The middle 60% belongs to the scene.
type: Two faces from one superfamily. Geist (41% of characters) at 600 for heads: 80px in the hero (5.6vw, leading 0.95, -0.04em), 76px chapter titles, 50px post-story heads; 29px leads at 500 and 17-19px body. Geist Mono (59%) at 11-12px uppercase, +0.06em, for the telemetry. Sentence case except the mono. The house version keeps Geist alone and sets the readout in sentence case at 16px with tabular figures.
colour: #000000 #0f0f0f #ffffff #7aebff #ff6666 #ffcb47 — A black page and near-black scene ground with white text, and three status accents with one job each: amber for observed and the detection boxes, coral for threat, cyan for secured, each under 5% of the text and never on chrome. The terrain brings olive and slate; the closing cards bring warm orange.
imagery: Real-time photoreal terrain in a cool, desaturated olive and slate grade with volumetric haze; a matte black flying-wing drone; flat 1px overlay props (bounding boxes with confidence labels, ID tags joined by dotted lines, a sensor cone, curved flight trails, ripple rings); a satellite-style photograph of a village; then warm sunset and dusk renders of a wildfire, a desert ridge and a substation as the payoff.
layout: One full-bleed sticky canvas carries 14 chapters over about 60,000px of runway (about 4500px each), with text docked in the corners at 32px margins: title top-left, lead bottom-left or bottom-right at most about 500px wide, telemetry bottom-right, chapter code top-centre. After the story the page returns to normal flow on black for an expanding three-card row and a split with a wireframe globe; margins drift from 32 to 40 to 48px. 72 screens for 435 words.

sections.description: The camera pulls back to three drones in a loose triangle, each with a small white ID tag, the tags joined by dotted lines; a 76px two-line title top-left and, bottom-right from x=732, a 29px lead over a four-row spec table with a label column and lighter values.

Detection: back over the terrain, about 25 small yellow bounding boxes (40-60px) with label chips naming an object class and a confidence percentage, the drone small at the centre, and a four-line readout bottom-right with coordinates, altitude, speed and counts.

A tactical map: a #0f0f0f ground with a faint perspective grid, an irregular outline of a land area covering about 40% of the width, a tag on its edge and three hotspots with 6s ripple rings. Over three chapters the hotspots and tag change colour (amber for survey, coral for threat, cyan for services on site) as grey drone glyphs fly in on curved trails.

After the dark story, three photographic renders in a row from x=48 to 1392 with 24px gaps: one open card 660px wide and two closed at 318px, all about 628px tall with about 10px corners, the open one carrying a 29px title and a three-line 15px description bottom-left.

steal: Tell a product's capability as one pinned scene: about 4500px of scroll per chapter, the camera moving continuously and the text still, changing only by opacity (out over 250ms, in over 400ms after a 200ms delay).

Give colour a job: three status accents, each tied to one state of the story and used only on tags, hotspots and single status words, never on chrome, each under 5% of the text, on black with white type.

After a cold, dark story, pay off with warm photographs in normal flow: an expanding row of three, one open at about 660px and two closed at about 318px. The site speaks in monospace telemetry over hairline grids; the house version sets the readout in the text face with tabular figures and lets the scene carry the structure.
media: One sticky full-bleed WebGL scene covers 100% of every story screen, with an SVG overlay drawing the boxes, tags, trails and ripple rings over it; after the story come three photographic mission cards and a wireframe globe bleeding off the right and bottom edges. Two canvases, four images, no video.
motion: A preloader of 4.5s or more shows only the dimmed model, then Lenis drives one pinned canvas through about 60,000px: the drone turns from banked to top-down, the camera pulls back to the formation, rises into the mesh, dives to a sensor view and cuts to the map, where zone colours change by chapter. Text moves by opacity only through 346 WAAPI fades (250ms ease-out, 400ms ease-in-out after 200ms), HUD marks transform over 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), 64 ripple rings loop on 6s, and there is no reduced-motion rule.

name: Maria Vasilyeva
idea: A designer's work treated as a playlist: every project is a track on one horizontal timeline, the wheel moves a playhead along it, and the track under the playhead blooms out of a thin strip of thumbnails into a scattered collage, with a hand-written layer of margin notes on top that can be switched off like the sound.
hero: One fixed 1440x900 off-white stage. Two near-black rails about 26px wide, inset 10px from the left and right edges, carry all the chrome as small vertical caps: name and role on the left reading upward, the menu and on/off toggles for sound and notes on the right. Seven faint lines every 112px divide the field into eight tracks; along the middle one runs a 32px strip of miniature thumbnails across the full width, the whole body of work in sequence, crossed by a thin vertical playhead. Around the playhead the current project's 10-20 images leave the strip and settle into an overlapping collage about 450-770px wide, with a small uppercase serif title and superscript year pinned to its upper-left corner. A hand-written scroll cue sits in a drawn oval at top centre (about 2.5vw), and a bottom row at y=868 gives the project number, name and link. No headline.
type: Three families. A high-contrast display serif (63% of characters) for project titles, uppercase at 29px (2vw), -0.02em, leading 1, with the year as a small superscript. A typewriter-style face (31%) for every small label at 13-15px. A loose hand-written script (6%) is the largest type on the page at 36.7px (2.5vw), used only for two notes. The house version drops the typewriter face for the text face and sets the label row in sentence case.
colour: #f9f9f9 #131313 #e9e9e9 #626262 — Strictly neutral: off-white ground on about 94% of the screen, near-black for the rails, the loader and text, a pale grey for the track lines, a mid grey for secondary text. Every hue arrives inside the project images: lavender product screens, deep greens, warm wood browns.
imagery: Case-study images of products and screens in mixed ratios (16:10 screens, portrait product shots), square corners, no shadows or filters, each keeping its own colour; pieces overlap freely and crop each other. Hand-drawn strokes, an oval round the scroll cue and a curling arrow to the project link, are the only illustration.
layout: No document scroll: a single stage whose content changes in place. The working field runs between the rails from x=48 to x=1390; the collage covers 30-50% of the width at a time and moves with the playhead, so 50-70% of the field is blank off-white, closed by the strip and the rails. A bottom row on a 4 | 1fr | 4 column grid. On the phone the rails become black bars at the top and bottom and the collage stacks above and below the strip.

sections.description: The loader: a near-black screen with the same faint tracks, a tiny percentage counter bottom centre, then groups of five short uppercase serif lines of music-themed loading phrases that slide in from the right over about 3.5s, each dragging a trail of its first letter repeated, before a 1.2s curtain reveals the stage.

The strip as the index: a 32px band of 30-60px thumbnails at the vertical centre, every project's images in sequence across the full width, with the playhead marking the current position; the bottom row repeats the same three facts for every project, number left, name centred, link right.

The notes layer: two hand-written notes at about 2.5vw drawn on with stroke-dashoffset, the scroll instruction in an oval at top centre and a note with a curling arrow pointing at the project link, both switchable from the right rail.

steal: Take the whole interface from one metaphor of the subject, here a playlist: a timeline strip, a playhead, a sound toggle and loader wording that all speak it, so nothing on the screen is filler.

Show the entire body of work at once as a thin thumbnail strip (about 3.5% of the height) and open only the current item into a large composition, so the index and the detail share one screen. The site rules the field with seven hairlines; the house version keeps the bands as space and lets the strip carry the structure.

Use a hand-written layer at about 2.5vw, drawn on with stroke-dashoffset, for at most two instructions (where to scroll, where to click), give it an off switch, and count it as one of the page's two faces.
media: One fixed WebGL canvas draws every image: a full-width 32px thumbnail strip plus one project's collage around the playhead, about 25-35% of the pixels in all, the rest off-white. No img or video elements; about 60-80 project images in the strip, 10-20 blooming per project.
motion: The loader runs past 4.5s: a counter alone for the first second, then serif lines slide in over 3.5s on cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.36,1) and a 1.2s curtain on (0.7,0.15,0.25,1) clears it. Each wheel step slides the playhead and pulls the next project out of the strip into a collage while the last collapses back, round an endless loop of seven; nearly everything else runs on cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), 1.4s for letter-spacing and transforms and 0.4s for fades, with no reduced-motion rule.

name: Michael Gatt
idea: A film composer shows his credits as a place you travel through: one WebGL camera flies down a corridor lined with stills from the shows and games he scored, then stops in a loose cloud of floating frames that is also the menu.
hero: A black sound gate first: one seven-word sentence stepped diagonally in tiny tracked caps (about 9px) asks for sound, with an opt-out link near the bottom edge. Then a fixed full-bleed canvas fades up from near black into a tunnel lined with about 35 dimmed stills from film, cartoons and games on its walls, ceiling and floor, receding to a vanishing point at the centre with the far planes lost in fog. At that point sits a centred four-line lockup about 450px wide: key words in 18px caps tracked 0.35em in white, joining words in about 10px grey small caps on the same baseline, saying this is a composer's world of film, TV and game music. No visible action until the wheel moves; a sound toggle sits bottom-right.
type: One family only: Zapf Humanist Demi, an Optima-like flared sans, in one weight, all caps, tracked 0.35em, leading 1.25. Two sizes and two tones make the hierarchy: 18px (1.2vw) white key words and 10-12px grey connectors and role lines. The largest word on the page is 1.2vw; the house version keeps the one flared face but sets the name at display size and nothing under 16px, in sentence case.
colour: #000000 #ffffff #969da0 — Black ground on about 90% of the pixels outside the stills, white for key words (77% of the text), a cool grey for connectors and secondary words. All other colour comes from the stills, dimmed to about half brightness.
imagery: Stills from the films, series, cartoons and games he scored, mostly landscape 16:9 to 4:3 with a few near-square, all given the same treatment: dimmed to about 50% against black, square corners, no borders or shadows, a slight Y rotation and perspective so they hang in space, the far planes fading into fog.
layout: One fixed full-bleed canvas under a thin HTML layer. Every word sits on the centre axis at x=720 in a clear vertical channel about 220px wide, with pictures pushed to the sides and corners at mixed depths. Wheel input moves the camera; scrollY stays 0. The end state is the hub: the wordmark about 60px from the top, an index toggle at mid-height, a two-line sentence nav about 40px above the bottom.

sections.description: After about two wheel steps the planes pull off the walls into a loose cloud of about twelve frames, 100-250px wide at mixed depths and turned up to about 10 degrees, round a clear centre column; two large frames bleed off the top-right and bottom-right corners. The wordmark with a small role line, an index toggle and the nav fade in on the axis.

The navigation written as one sentence, about 300px wide over two lines: three destination words in 18px tracked caps in white, the joining words in about 10px grey small caps on the same baseline, the last destination alone on the second line with an underline as the primary action.

steal: Over a full-screen picture stage, put every word on one centre axis and keep a clear channel about 15% of the viewport wide free of pictures; push the pictures to the sides and corners at mixed depths and let one or two crop off the corners so the scene reads as bigger than the screen.

Keep a camera flight short, about two steps from the welcome state to a settled end state, and make that end state the menu. The site drives it from the wheel with no page scroll; here the page scrolls natively and the flight is tied to a sticky stage that ends.

Dim every picture in a dark scene to about 50-60% brightness and fade the far ones into the ground, so white type stays readable with no scrim. The site sets every word at 8-18px in tracked caps; under the house rules the title is large and nothing is under 16px.
media: One fixed WebGL canvas covers 100% of the screen and holds every picture as a textured plane: about 35 lining a tunnel to a central vanishing point, then about 12 floating round a clear text channel. No img or video elements in the DOM.
motion: After the sound gate the scene fades up from about 10% brightness over 1-2s while the lockup arrives letter by letter; wheel steps then dolly the camera down the tunnel and pull the planes out into the cloud, ending after about two steps. Links fade from grey to white over 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) and widen their tracking over 0.4s; no GSAP or Lenis, and no reduced-motion rule.

name: Miu Miu A House That We Shaped
idea: A bag campaign set inside one furnished room, a period salon with hand-painted vermilion and emerald doors rendered in real time: you find the products by touching objects in the room rather than by scrolling, so the house is the interface and the brand mood comes from the paint on the set.
hero: An entry gate on a flat deep navy field: a centred white block about 500px wide, a 26px bold uppercase kicker and three 58px (≈4vw) bold uppercase title lines at a 108px pitch, each force-justified so the words hug both edges and the last word is letter-spaced across the full measure; then a two-line 14px deck, a small sound notice at the top and a light Enter button about 100x48 at the bottom centre, a spinner until 1.2s. After Enter the room fills the screen: the camera opens tight on a hand-painted vermilion door and pulls back over a few seconds to the wide set while yellow subtitle lines cross-fade; then one pulsing hotspot on a notebook and a 273x100 paper-beige card at the bottom centre name the first task. No header, logo or menu.
type: Work Sans alone at 400 and 700. The gate title in bold uppercase at about 58px, force-justified; after entry the largest text is 16px (1.1vw) regular, leading 1.2, black on paper beige in the task card, and subtitles are about 14px in yellow. Type is fluid from a root unit of about 10px at 1440. The gate title runs to four lines; under the house rules it is two.
colour: #0c0f60 #ffffff #948c89 #7c6958 #776453 #fcf5e6 #ffe100 — Gate: navy at 100% with white type. Room: a greige wall (about 45%), a taupe dado (31%) and a mushroom carpet (24%), with two painted doors, vermilion (about 8%) and emerald (about 5%), carrying all the brand colour and a mustard lamp shade as a small accent. The interface is one warm paper beige with black text.
imagery: A photoreal but soft real-time set with a matte, slightly underexposed, low-contrast filmic grade: doors in rough hand-brushed paint with the frame showing through the strokes, and a red paint stroke along the dado rail like unfinished work. The canvas has no corners or frame. Product pictures arrive later as a scattered collage of rotated portrait figures (from the stylesheet, not captured).
layout: No document flow: exactly one 1440x900 viewport, scrollY 0 on all twelve wheel steps. The gate centres a 500px block with about 470px of navy either side. In the room the wall runs to y≈406, the dado to y≈686 and the carpet below; the hero door stands just left of centre and the second door is cut by the right edge. The interface is four docked pieces on under 3% of the frame.

sections.description: The intro film: the camera starts tight on the vermilion door, a lamp vignette at the left and an armchair at the right, and pulls back over a few seconds to the wide room while three short manifesto lines cross-fade as a 14px yellow subtitle about 52px above the bottom.

The resting room as the interface: the vermilion door (about 266x600) at x≈590-856, a lamp and a table of stacked notebooks on the left, the armchair on the right, the emerald door in perspective on the side wall. One pulsing white hotspot about 36px with a 70px ring sits on the notebook, the task card names it, and a 44px sound toggle sits 20px from the bottom-right corner.

The end page, known from the stylesheet only: five portrait figures of about 3:4 scattered with rotations from -47 to 9 degrees like photographs thrown on a table, with a fluid end title and lines that underline one after another.

steal: Put the colour in the set, not the interface: keep about 90% of the frame in muted greige, taupe and mushroom, let two saturated accents on objects carry the brand mood, and keep the interface to one warm paper tone with black text.

Open with a camera pull-back from tight on the hero object to the wide resting composition over a few seconds, and fade the first task in only when the camera settles (opacity 0.5s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1)); place the hero object just off centre and crop a second one by the frame edge so the room continues past the screen.

When the page is a scene, limit the interface to a few docked pieces covering under 3% of the frame: one subtitle line, one task card, one hotspot on the object to touch, one sound toggle. Under the house rules the first screen still names the product and offers a plain route to the collection.
media: The gate is pure type on navy; after entry one fixed WebGL canvas renders the whole room at 100% of the viewport from the first frame, with no img or video elements in the captured state and the interface on under 3% of the frame. The intro is a camera move inside the scene, not a video.
