motion: Twelve wheel steps leave the room unchanged apart from a sway of up to about 18px, while the camera pull-back plays on its own clock and then the hotspot ring pulses from scale 1 to 2.2 over 2s cubic-bezier(.215,.61,.355,1) as the task card fades in over 0.55-0.65s. Most moves use easeOutQuint (.23,1,.32,1, 37 uses) or expo-out (.16,1,.3,1) for 1.6s mask wipes, and the pulse, wiggle and jitter loops run with no reduced-motion rule after a 4.2s load.

name: twks
idea: A Geneva agency site set like a Swiss printed sheet: the fold is a black field with the navigation as one horizon line across the exact middle, broken by a single gold object from a client project that turns slowly; then an indented statement, the work on a tight 10px grid, and a fixed black footer where an animal drawn in tiny characters prowls.
hero: Black 1440x900 with nothing but one photographed gold oval seal, about 250x180 (17% of the width), dead centre and turning slowly on a turntable loop, and one 20px lowercase white line at y=450 on a 6-column grid: the brand at x=10, four section links from x≈247, a three-word descriptor of the kind of agency from x≈953 and the contact link flush right. The line runs into the object and continues on the other side. No headline and no button; about 3-4% of the screen is lit and the black is the composition.
type: One family, GT Standard, a Swiss neo-grotesk at 400/500/600, in effectively two sizes: 52.8px (3.7vw) at 600, leading 1.0, -0.01em, for the statement only, and 20px (1.4vw) at 400, leading 1.2, +0.01em, for everything else. Hierarchy comes from a grey rather than more sizes; the ratio is about 2.6.
colour: #ffffff #000000 #8c8c8c — White ground (84%) and black for the fold and footer; text in black, with one grey for descriptors, links and inactive options (about 3.4:1 on white, below AA at 20px; the house version darkens it to about #6f6f6f). No accent: the client work supplies every hue.
imagery: Client work only: photographed objects and campaign images in acid yellow, pastel stickers, orange, gold on black. Three ratios (3:2, 3:4, 1:1), 0px radius, object-fit cover, no filters, and muted looping clips sized exactly like the image tiles. An animal drawn by script from tiny white characters in the footer.
layout: 10px outer margins and 10px gutters on a 6-column grid of about 226px: 2-up tiles of 698px, 4-up tiles of 344px. The statement's first line is indented exactly one column so it starts under the nav's first link. Sections sit about 130-200px apart. The case grid pairs a 3:2 with a 3:4 tile per row, top-aligned, which leaves a 698x465 white hole under the shorter one. A fixed black footer is uncovered as the white page slides away.

sections.description: Four lines at 52.8px (3.7vw), weight 600, black on white, running nearly the full width with the first line indented one grid column (about 236px) so it lines up with the nav's first link; a small inline glyph stands in for one space.
A small label in column 2 and an eight-line 20px paragraph in columns 5 and 6 (about 462px) with a 75px first-line indent, then two link rows, each a 20px word at the left and an arrow at the right.

Four case tiles in two 698px columns with a 10px gutter, a checkerboard of 3:2 and 3:4 that swaps sides on the second row, one of them a muted autoplaying 3:4 video; under each, 8px below, a 20px client name in black over a 20px one-line descriptor in grey.

A fixed full-viewport black sheet uncovered as the white page slides up by its own height: a four-column information band in the top 40% (contact, an empty column, socials and language, address), and in the bottom 55% an animal about 350x150 built from tiny white characters that assembles from a scatter and walks slowly.

steal: Let the navigation be the fold: one 20px line across the exact vertical centre of a dark screen, broken by a single real object about 17% of the width that turns slowly. Under the house rules the first screen also needs a clear h1, so set the name and what the agency does in two lines beside the object.

Use one family and two sizes, about 20px for everything and one display size near 3.7vw, and build hierarchy from position and size rather than extra sizes or pale greys, keeping running text in the full ink; indent the statement's first line by exactly one grid column so it lines up with the nav. At that size the house rules want the statement as a two-line headline or a paragraph of 36px or less.

Keep 10px margins and gutters with square corners so the work reads like a contact sheet, pair a 3:2 with a 3:4 tile per row and swap sides on the next, and caption each in two 20px lines (name, descriptor). Close the gap under the shorter tile with its caption or a quotation; the site leaves it white.
media: The fold is a black field with one small turning object at the centre, about 3-4% of the screen lit; the work then sits in a 2-up checkerboard of 3:2 and 3:4 tiles and a 4-up strip of squares with one taller tile breaking the baseline, captions underneath. Seven images and three short muted loops sized exactly like the tiles; a glyph-drawn animal animates the footer.
motion: No preloader: the fold is complete at 400ms and only the object turns, face-on to edge-on over about 4s. Lenis and five ScrollTriggers sink and dim the hero on two scrubs and slide the white page away to uncover the fixed footer, labels rise with autoAlpha and y over 1.8s power4.out at a 0.1 stagger, arrows rotate over 0.5s power4.out, and the sticky nav's difference blend collides with busy pictures; there is no reduced-motion rule.

name: Vectr
idea: An industrial staffing service tells its process as a flight over a miniature clay world: one fixed WebGL diorama of plants, warehouses, wind turbines and tiny workers in a single matte pale blue that matches the page ground, crossed by a glowing blue trail that runs from a headquarters building past a campus and a grid of work positions and ends at the brand mark itself.
hero: On a pale steel-blue ground, a fixed full-viewport canvas in the same colour, its fog fading into the page so the scene has no edge: an isometric matte miniature industrial town (tower blocks, a warehouse, wind turbines, crates, tiny figures) fills the lower ~60%, cropped by the bottom and right edges. In the open fog above, a two-line 96px (6.7vw) headline, weight 500, -0.06em, leading 0.9, is centred and about 700px wide from y≈115, with a three-line 18px subline at y≈350 doing the real explaining. A transparent 80px nav: two small links at the left, the wordmark centred, a frosted apply pill and a near-black request pill at the right; an underlined scroll prompt at the bottom centre.
type: Roboto alone at 400 and 500: a 96px hero (6.7vw, -0.06em, leading 0.9), an 80px closing line, 64px section headlines (-0.04em), 36px footer cells, 24px step and FAQ titles, 18px body (the bulk of the characters), and 12-14px uppercase nav and button labels. All the typographic character comes from a custom extended geometric wordmark, used at about 90px in the nav and 1344px wide in the footer.
colour: #d0e1eb #fcfcfc #050419 #585765 #3932dc — Pale steel blue for the first 43% of the page (canvas and fog), then white, then near-black indigo for the closing call and the footer. Text is mostly a muted slate (about 4.6:1 on the blue, less over the model; the house rules want running text in the full ink). One electric indigo for the logo, the footer arrows and the light trail; a red beam is the only warm signal.
imagery: A monochrome clay render: every object matte pale blue-white with soft ambient-occlusion shadows and low contrast, colour kept for signals (a cyan-to-indigo light trail, a dot glow under the active area, a red incoming beam, the indigo mark). Black isometric pictograms at the camera's angle for the features, and one warm photograph of three hard-hatted workers on a gantry, with about 12px corners, that breaks the world.
layout: 18px nav insets; content at 40 or 48px margins. The fixed canvas sits behind the first ~4700px, with a 900px sticky stage over 3.8 screens for four steps and a pinned feature row over 3.3 screens, then normal flow: a photo split (656x400 picture at x=40, text from x=830), a two-half FAQ, a dark closing block and a three-cell footer row at a 480px pitch. 12.1 screens for 326 words.

sections.description: A 900px sticky stage where the camera stops at four vignettes: the headquarters building wearing the logo, taking in a red beam and sending out the blue trail; a hangar campus the trail sweeps through; a field of white square tiles with one raised and a figure on it; and finally the brand mark as a glowing indigo object in a halo of cyan dots. The step list is docked bottom-left at x=48 in a column about 600px wide: inactive steps as 14px rows, the active one with a 24px title and an 18px body.

A white panel slides up over the canvas with a two-line 64px headline at x=40, and a row of four 350px cards fills in one per scroll step, each with a black isometric pictogram, a 20px title and a short 14px body.

Split: a warm photograph of three workers in hi-vis on a plant gantry, 656x400 (46% of the width), at the left margin, and from x=830 a three-line 64px headline, a two-line paragraph and a dark 48px pill, the group centred on the picture.

A near-black indigo block: an 80px two-line closing line at x=40 with a white pill under it, a full-width row of three 480x200 cells each with a 36px page name and an electric-blue arrow, then the extended wordmark in white across 93% of the width and a 12px legal row.

steal: Set a WebGL scene's clear colour and fog to the exact page ground, render the whole world in one matte clay tone, and keep colour for two or three signals: one bright trail, one contrasting incoming beam, the brand colour on the mark.

Tell an N-step process as N camera stops in one persistent scene, about 0.95 screens of scroll per step, the step list docked bottom-left and the focal object centre-right, and end the last stop on the brand mark so the journey has a destination. The site numbers its steps; the house version shows order by position and by the active step's size.

Let one neutral grotesk do all the reading and give the personality to a custom extended wordmark, repeated across 93% of the width to close the footer. The site's four icon-topped feature cards drop back into a generic kit; the house version keeps the world going with a section blueprint instead.
media: One fixed WebGL canvas covers 100% of the first screen, the clay town in the lower ~60% and fog in the ground colour above it, and stays behind the first ~4700px as camera stops for the steps; then one 656x400 photograph in a split, four 96px pictograms and a giant SVG wordmark. No video.
motion: A 2.5-4s CSS loader turns the mark from -60 degrees to 0 over 1.5s and draws two orbits over about 2s, then hero lines rise and fade over 1.5s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) at 0.1-0.5s staggers after the canvas fades in over 0.7s. Lenis moves the camera between four stops, swapping step copy over 0.5s on the same expo-out curve (44 uses in all) and opening the active body by grid-template-rows over 0.6s, while the pinned feature row adds one card per step; there is no reduced-motion rule.

name: LPAS
idea: An architecture and interiors practice organised by market sector: each of five sectors gets its own earthy ground colour, like swatches from a material board, and the sectors slide as a card rail over a fixed, dimmed video of the studio; a 45-degree corner cut taken from the logo is the one shape motif.
hero: After a charcoal loader of about 4.5s with four stacked process verbs, a full-bleed muted studio video at half brightness fills the screen. A thin wordmark top-left at 50px, a small dark menu pill top-right. The headline, 75px (5.2vw, leading 1.0) in three lines about 800px wide, is docked bottom-left with its last baseline about 65px above the bottom edge, and three 14px labels (discipline, approach, a scroll cue with a 30px circle arrow) sit exactly on the vertical centre line. A 200px sliver of the first sector card already shows at the right edge as the cue to continue. The headline arrives last, about 5s in.
type: Aeonik alone, almost entirely at 400 with 600 for small labels, sentence case throughout. A short scale: 75px display (5.2vw, leading 1.0), 56px for the credo and rail titles (3.9vw, leading 1.1), 50px for the closing list, 38 and 28px section titles, 16 and 14px body, 12px captions. Fluid sizes by clamp() on a 10px root.
colour: #ffffff #262626 #111111 #625653 #925434 #c9d3df #707569 #e3c1aa — White page, charcoal for the loader and footer, near-black text (though 65% of the characters are set in mid-grey #747474). Five sector grounds of similar value and low chroma (taupe, rust, pale blue-grey, sage, peach), each with a lighter tint for hover; no other accent.
imagery: Bright architectural photography with blue skies and dusk light, its brick and timber tones echoing the sector palette, and a 61s documentary-feeling studio video as the hero. Square corners, one 8:5 ratio for projects, no filters; the hero and the closing photo are dimmed to about 50% for white text, and pictures are oversized in their frames so they can drift.
layout: 50px margins and a 1340px measure on a 20-column main grid with 10px gutters. A fixed hero overtaken by a pinned horizontal rail (about 4320px of scroll), then a statement, a mirrored mosaic, a news list, a full-bleed photo band and a sticky footer uncovered like a curtain. Section gaps of about 100-140px. The ground changes by section: white, each sector colour, white, charcoal.

sections.description: Five sector cards, each about 770px wide (53.5vw), slide left over the dimmed hero: a photograph on the top 68% and a flat sector-colour panel on the bottom 32%, holding the sector name at 56px bottom-left with a 30px inset, a two-line 16px descriptor right-aligned and a 45px outline circle-plus button top-right. The incoming card's photo grows from about 450 to 615px tall as it centres; neighbours peek about 270px on the left and 400px on the right.
A three-line 56px credo about 647px wide at the top-left; below it a 14px label in a narrow left column and a 16px paragraph about 800px wide starting at x=388, closed by an underlined text link.

Six 8:5 images in two mirrored rows: one large (about 678x424, 47% of the width) beside two small ones (334x209), then two small ones bottom-aligned on the left under a placed void, with the large one on the right. The first large image has its top-left corner cut at 45 degrees by 60px and the last its bottom-right, so the cuts bracket the group. Each image carries a 16px name and a 12px place beneath it.

A full-bleed dimmed interior photograph carrying the five sector names stacked at 50px in white scrolls away to uncover a sticky 625px charcoal footer with two office addresses, social links and a back-to-top link.

steal: Give each content category its own flat ground drawn from one material family at similar value and low chroma, each with a lighter tint for hover, and keep the rest of the page white plus one charcoal, so the colours read as a system and not as decoration.

Take one shape from the logo and use it sparingly: a 45-degree corner cut of 20-60px on a single corner of selected images, alternating top-left on the first and bottom-right on the last so the cuts bracket a group.

Stagger a two-row mosaic big-small-small, then small-small-big, with the small pair bottom-aligned to the tall neighbour so the void above them is placed; keep one ratio and caption every image in 16px. The site's 75px hero headline runs to three lines; under the house rules cut it to two.
media: A 61s muted studio video at 50% brightness covers the whole first screen and stays fixed while a rail of photo-over-colour cards slides over it; projects sit in a mirrored 8:5 mosaic, and a full-bleed dimmed photo band carries the closing list. Thirteen media elements in all, no canvas or WebGL.
motion: Under Lenis the sector rail pins for about 4320px and travels about 836px per 900px of wheel while the incoming photo grows and pictures drift inside oversized frames. Project images wipe in with clip-path inset and opacity over 1.2s cubic-bezier(0.14,0.83,0.4,1), hovers take .3s cubic-bezier(0,0,.13,.99), the headline rises through a mask after the 4.5s loader, and there is no reduced-motion rule.

name: Lacoste Polo Factory
idea: A brand playground that frames the making of one shirt as a toy factory you tour: the landing is a single fixed stage where the brand's own goods, 3D polos in five garment colours and stitched crocodile patches, burst out of an embossed crest every time you turn the wheel.
hero: One fixed 1440x900 stage: a pale sage ground with mint rays only 4-6% lighter swirling out from the centre, a full-screen 3D canvas on top. A narrow centred stack about 475px tall on the viewport's middle line: a 24px welcome line, the title in two lines at 48px bold (3.3vw, leading 0.83) in bottle green, an embossed 3D medallion about 245x170 carrying the crest, a three-line 12px paragraph at a 400px measure, and one white 244x78 button with the label left and a dark green arrow chip right. Around it 8-16 matte 3D polos (110-130px) and stitched patches tumble outward and crop at the frame. Corners at a 24px inset: a menu pill top-left, a sound pill top-right, a 234px butter-yellow prize-draw card bottom-right that tilts on a 3s loop.
type: One custom brand family in 400, 400 italic and 700. A 48px bold title (leading 0.83), a 24px regular welcome line, 18px for the button label and card copy, then 14, 13 and 12px; 12px is by far the commonest size and sets the hero paragraph. Sentence case for the title, uppercase for buttons. Sizes scale from a 40px base variable, with no clamp or vw.
colour: #d0dfbe #e1ffc2 #0b4221 #ffffff #fcf383 #4a4938 — Pale sage with mint rays on about 85% of the screen, bottle green for all text and chips, white for the button and pills, butter yellow for the promo card. The loader and the tour stations add more brand pairs (denim with sky blue, blush with red, olive with yellow), and the 3D objects bring garment green, chocolate and salmon. The house version drops the rays for flat sage.
imagery: Soft, matte, toy-like renders of the brand's own products: slightly stylised polos and crocodile patches with raised stitch dots, soft contact shadows, no outlines or gloss, and a pillowy embossed medallion. One small oval-masked photograph of polo fabric in the promo card.
layout: No scrolling sections: one fixed stage, scrollY stays 0. The text stack takes about 28% of the width (columns 9 to 16) on the centre line; the rest is stage space for the 3D burst, with chrome docked in three corners at a 24px inset. On the phone the medallion moves up to about 39% of the height and all the text docks to the bottom with a full-width 58px button.

sections.description: The loader: a solid colour ground with an outline crest about 206x140 (14% of the width) centred and a two-line caption pinned near the bottom. Every 1-2s the ground and the crest swap together through brand colour pairs (olive with yellow, mint with green, blush with red, denim with sky), with hard cuts, so the wait previews the palette.

The promo card docked bottom-right: 234x236 in butter yellow, an oval-masked fabric photograph, a round arrow chip and an 18px four-line contest line; it opens a centred sign-up dialog with seven fields, full-screen below 1023px.

Behind the start button and not captured: a tour of four stations (start, knitting, dyeing, embroidering), each with its own pale machine tint, hotspots that pop in from scale 0 through 1.15 to 1 over 0.4s, and drag-to-rotate cursors.

steal: Use the brand's own products as the moving matter: real colourways of the goods and the logo patch as matte textured 3D objects, 8-16 per frame, where abstract shapes would read as generic. Keep them out of a central lane about 420px wide; the site lets them cross the title, and the house rules let nothing lie on a headline.
Turn an unavoidable load into a palette preview: a solid ground and the mark swapping colour together through four or five brand pairs every 1-2s, hard cuts, the caption pinned near the bottom.
Dock all text to the bottom on the phone, with a full-width 56px button and 24px gutters, and move the moving object up to about 39% of the height, so the stage stays above the thumb.
media: Media covers the whole first screen: a fixed ray-pattern ground, a full-screen 3D canvas in which 8-16 products take about 15-25% of the frame, and the embossed medallion set inside the type stack. The only photograph is a 200x106 oval in the promo card; no video.
motion: The wheel never scrolls the page: each step fires a fresh burst of polos and patches from the medallion that tumble outward, grow and leave past the edges, with no new content and no progress cue. The loader cuts between colourways every 1-2s for more than 4.5s; buttons spring on cubic-bezier(.175,.885,.32,1.275) at 0.2-0.3s (an overshoot the house motion layer does not use), the promo card shakes on a 3s loop, and there is no reduced-motion rule.

name: OFFFForum
idea: Two events and two voices: the loud festival half of the name in a blunt geometric grotesk mark and the talks day in a classical flared-serif caps word, locked into one wordmark and laid over a fast documentary slideshow of past editions, so the page reads like an event poster that changes every second or two.
hero: A full-bleed documentary photograph of a past edition (speakers at microphones, a crowd under a projected logo) fills the screen under a dark scrim heaviest at the bottom, and changes every 1.5-2s with a 0.5s crossfade. The wordmark, 688x88 (48% of the width), is pinned 16px from the top-left, with a three-cell fact box under it (event, dates, venue) in 18px bold grotesk, leading 0.94. A 45px (3.1vw) serif-caps statement over four centred lines, about 47% of the width, sits in the lower third, with a small white pill ticket button about 210x26 under it; two tiny links sit top-right. The middle 400px holds no text.
type: Two families mapped to the two events. A custom flared glyphic serif at 400, caps, -0.02em, for the statement (45px, leading 0.96) and all the small UI labels; a tight grotesk at 600, -0.04em, leading 0.94-0.97, for the facts and the 32px newsletter heading. The footer wordmark is the largest type at about 12.6vw. Fixed rem tokens per breakpoint. The statement runs to four lines; under the house rules it is two.
colour: #000000 #ffffff #c5c5c5 — Strict black and white: black under the hero (about 64% of the first scroll), a white footer, grey only for legal text. All colour comes from the photography: warm stage reds and oranges, cool blue light. The scrim under the hero text is the one darkening the house rules allow on a photograph.
imagery: Candid, slightly underexposed event photography with warm stage light and natural colour, no duotone or grain: speakers, crowds, hands and objects. Square corners on all media; the only rounded shapes are the pill button and the social chips.
layout: One 16px outer margin governs everything, so the 1408px footer wordmark lines up exactly with the header logo. The page is only 1.6 screens: a 900px black hero, then a 497px white footer on an implied 24-column grid (heading in columns 1-7, links from the centre line, social chips at the right). No section rhythm beyond the black-then-white flip.

sections.description: A white block about 55% of the viewport tall: a three-line 32px bold grotesk newsletter invitation in the left 30% with two audience choices, link columns in small serif caps from the centre line, outlined social chips at the right; after about 110px of open white the black wordmark runs edge to edge inside the margins (1408x181, ratio 7.8:1) above a single legal row.

steal: When a brand has two parts, give each its own face (a heavy geometric grotesk at 600 and a classical serif in caps at 400), lock them side by side in one wordmark and carry the split into the type tokens; it stays inside the two-face limit.

For a people-driven event, run a fast documentary slideshow as the hero: two stacked image layers, a 0.5s opacity crossfade, a new photograph every 1.5-2s, and what, when and where docked under the logo at 18px bold. The site boxes the facts in 1px rules; the house version sets them as three plain columns.

End a short page with the wordmark running the full width inside the same 16px margin as the header logo, so the footer itself is the finale. Give the ticket button at least 44px of height and 16px text; the site's 26px pill is easy to miss on a busy photograph.
media: The photograph covers 100% of the first screen as two stacked cover layers crossfading in place under a scrim, with at least eight photographs seen across the captures; the footer's only picture is the wordmark. No video on the home page.
motion: No preloader: the page is painted by 400ms and the only motion is the slideshow, a new photograph every 1.5-2s with a 0.5s ease opacity crossfade. Lenis runs on a page only 497px deep, with no pins, reveals or split text; UI moves on power2-out cubic-bezier(.32,.94,.6,1) at .3-.4s and quart-out (.25,1,.5,1) at .6s.

name: 20 Years Inspired by People
idea: A studio marks its twentieth year by turning the spotlight round: instead of its own work it collects what inspired it, so the home is a single night-sky door with one reversed sentence and one button into an archive of contributed stories.
hero: One fixed 1440x900 screen that never scrolls. A fullscreen WebGL field in deep teal-black with two soft glow pools in the lower third, sparse star dots, grain and the odd thin diagonal streak, darkened by vignette bands 100px deep at top and bottom and 200px at the sides. The header is corners only: a small slash wordmark at x=64, a language switch 64px from the right. Dead centre, its midpoint within 10px of the viewport middle and about 41% of the width: a tiny tracked line with the founding year, a two-line narrow serif headline at ~92px (6.4vw) with two key words underlined in mint, two lines of 12px body, and one solid mint button about 256x44 placed over the brightest glow. Text covers 1.8% of the screen.
type: Two families. A narrow high-contrast serif at weight 400 for the headline (~92px, 6.4vw, leading 1.0, sentence case, centred) and for archive titles at 24px; a geometric variable sans (DM Sans class) at 12-13px for body and the button label, on a 22px line pitch. Headline to body about 7:1, with no bold anywhere. Body at 12px sits below the house floor of 16px.
colour: #0a0a0a #091d1c #152524 #114d4e #ededed #00ffc2 — A deep teal-black ground (about 70% of the screen) with mint-teal glow (about 25%) and off-white type. One saturated mint accent kept under 1% of the screen: the button fill, two thin underlines, the logo slash and a caret.
imagery: No photograph on the home. The only picture is a living colour-and-light field drawn in WebGL; the archive of contributor portraits (30 square thumbnails on a slowly turning ring) sits behind the button.
layout: One fixed viewport with 64px header gutters and a single centred stack; no sections and no scroll. About 60% of the width is atmosphere on either side of the text, closed by the corner header items and the edge vignettes. On the phone the stack keeps its order inside ~58px margins, the headline drops to ~37px (9.5vw) and the menu becomes a 48px outlined square docked bottom-right.

sections.description: Behind the button, measured rather than seen: an archive of contributed stories as 30 square 120px portraits on a ring that turns on a 72s linear loop, with story titles in the serif at 24px, leading 1.04, left-aligned.
A share form reached from the menu, five fields, where visitors add what once inspired them; the menu also lists a manifesto, a visit page and credits, set at 48px serif on the phone.

steal: For a single-message entrance, centre the whole stack so its midpoint sits within about 10px of the viewport centre at about 40% of the width, and let the rest of the screen be one field. The site uses a glowing WebGL gradient; the house version is a flat dark ground or a real night photograph.

Spend the accent on the button alone and keep it under 1% of the screen, so the button is the only bright block. The site also underlines two headline words in the accent, which the house rules ban: let the words carry the emphasis.

Bring a short headline in word by word, then the body, then the button only once it settles. The site resolves each word from blur (filter 0.38s ease-out, opacity 0.5s cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1)); the house version uses opacity with a 16-24px rise, and keeps any loader under 2s.
media: One fixed fullscreen WebGL colour field covers 100% of the first screen and is the only picture. Text sits on its darker upper middle with no scrim, the brightest glow pool is placed under the button, and every real image is kept behind one click.
motion: After a black loader that shows only a dot for over 4.5s, the headline resolves word by word from blur to sharp (84 split characters; opacity 0.5s cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1), filter 0.38s ease-out). After that only ambient drift and an 8s stepped grain loop move; the home ignores the wheel (scrollY stays 0) and a cursor lens smears the letters it rests on.

name: Hearst Exhibit 2026
idea: A joint photography show from two fashion magazines presented as an archive thrown into the air: dozens of covers whirl through black space as bending paper, then two land flat and become the doors to the two galleries.
hero: Black at load. At about 1.2s a centred three-line serif lockup steps in word by word, the last line, the place name, widest at about 6vw (85-90px) and the block about 525px across, with a thin script connective written between the first two lines and a tiny two-line venue caption at bottom centre. By 2.5s it blurs away and magazine covers spiral up out of the lower right as bending paper planes. In the settled screen the only text is a 19px two-line question centred at y=80-125, and below it two 3:4 covers (280x373, 80px apart, the pair 44% of the width) landed side by side as the choice, with about 200px of black above and below and 400px on each side. No title, dates or nav remain.
type: Ivy Presto, a light high-contrast Didone-like serif (100-400), for the lockup: the place line at about 6vw (13vw on the phone), the two names at about 52px, a small article at about 25px, stepped left, right and full width. Instrument Sans 400 at about 19px (1.3vw), leading 1.25, slightly negative tracking, centred, for the instruction. A fluid clamp scale runs between 375 and 1920px viewports: display 50-100px, body 16-20px.
colour: #000000 #ffffff — Black ground on about 95% of the screen and white type on under 1%. Every other colour comes from the photographs: a red bow on one cover, a teal-green field on the other, skin tones.
imagery: Untouched magazine cover photography in the true 3:4 ratio, square corners, no filter, rendered as WebGL paper planes that curl in flight and unroll flat when they land. A full-screen film-grain layer flickers over everything.
layout: One fixed 1440x900 stage with no document scroll. Everything sits on the vertical axis at x=720; the real content occupies roughly columns 7 to 18, and the symmetric black void reads as a dark gallery wall around two framed prints. On the phone the covers stack at about 65% of the width with a 22px gap so both fit one screen.

sections.description: The transition: a full-viewport canvas in which dozens of covers fly as paper that bends and twists, rising in a spiral from the lower right and shrinking as they recede, packed into the right half and covering 10-20% of the screen at any moment.
The two galleries sit behind the covers and were not captured; the stylesheet carries a character-reveal keyframe and several more display faces that are presumably used inside.

steal: Make the transition literal to the subject: printed matter rendered as paper that bends in flight and unrolls flat when it lands in its slot, with square corners and the true cover ratio.

For a two-way choice, centre two 3:4 pictures 80px apart at about 44% of the width with at least 200px of clear ground above and below, so they read as prints on a wall. Under the house rules each door also carries its name in text, and the screen keeps the title, dates and venue.
Let the photographs be the only colour: a black ground, white type and nothing else in the palette, so the two covers glow like lit prints on a dark wall.
media: During the intro the canvas covers 100% of the screen but the flying covers fill only about 15%, packed into the right half; the settled chooser shows two covers on about 16% of the viewport with the rest black. No video; about a dozen further covers exist only as WebGL textures.
motion: Lockup words fade in over 800ms on cubic-bezier(0.65,0.05,0.36,1) at delays from 1000 to 2500ms while a script connective writes itself in eight strokes; the lockup leaves with opacity and a 0-6px blur over 800ms, the covers storm in, and the question arrives over 1200ms on cubic-bezier(0.77,0,0.18,1). About 5s pass before the choice can be made, with no skip and no reduced-motion rule, and a grain layer jitters at 0.15s steps forever.

name: Meer Mohsin
idea: A front-end developer's portfolio told as a dark ritual: one red neo-tribal sigil rendered in 3D splits, merges, crumples and stretches from screen to screen, and every statement pairs hard grotesk capitals with a single word in a formal copperplate script, on black and blood red.
hero: A red preloader of about 2.5s (#990000 with grain, a huge black script counter running 000 to 100) fades to black. The settled fold is pure black with only the two mirrored halves of a red 3D tribal emblem, each about 300x370 (21% of the width), placed symmetrically either side of the centre, and a dim progress bar bottom-left: no name, title, nav or action. On the first scroll the halves merge over a centred headline: two grotesk cap lines at about 195px (13.5vw; the longer about 66% of the width) with one script word wedged between them, overlapping both by about a third of the cap height, all in bright red. Only on the second screen does the visitor learn that this person builds websites.
type: Three families. A neutral grotesk in regular (61% of characters) and light (34%) for caps statements, a 30px light uppercase paragraph, 18px stat lines, 36px project names and a 66px sentence-case statement. A formal copperplate script (5%) for single words and numerals only: the counter, 70px stat figures, 150px service words, a 156px awards heading and a 228px (15.8vw) footer marquee. Body 18px. The house version keeps each headline in one face and gives the script a role of its own, never an accent word inside a headline.
colour: #000000 #990000 #d60407 #ffffff #f5f5f5 — Black page on about 70% of the screens, blood red for full grounds (about 12% of the area) and much of the text, a brighter red for display type, white for chrome and labels. Deep red on black and black on deep red measure only about 2.35:1, too weak for reading copy. The project mockups bring purple and amber from outside the system.
imagery: Gothic pictures (faces, an eye, a falling figure, TV static) pushed into a red duotone with heavy grain; flat illustrated flame silhouettes and white torn-paper edges as the boundaries between black and red grounds; glossy full-colour device mockups in the work section. Square corners throughout.
layout: Mostly symmetric about the vertical axis on full-bleed grounds, with a logo glyph at (42,25) and a fixed bottom bar that divides the width into thirds with three mood-word labels. Three long pins of about 5440, 4560 and 4440px stretch 295 words over 31 screens. Ground changes happen through illustrated flame and torn-paper edges 630-680px tall, never straight cuts.

sections.description: The emblem crumples into a spiky mass at the centre while a full-bleed band of red flame silhouettes rises from the bottom and turns the ground red; four lines of 30px light uppercase in deep red run from x=72 to 1348, the words drifting in from scattered offsets.

Pinned for about 6 screens: a full-viewport line diagram in dark red (corner diagonals, a centred square about 600px, a diamond, both axes) round a centred deck of ten stacked 216x270 duotone pictures that flips at every step, one huge red script word laid across the deck on the horizon, and a three- or four-item skills list in 16px red that types itself out at the right.

A 259x270 red card with a falling figure grows into a full-width red band about 600px tall with torn-paper edges, and its 66px black sentence (4.6vw, three lines, one word swapped into the script) scales up with it.

A pinned vertical carousel: the current project as a 648x450 mockup photograph (45% of the width), the previous and next as 194x135 thumbnails directly above and below, a blurred, darkened copy of the current picture filling the ground, the 36px name at x=72 on the centre line and a 12px description at the right.

steal: Give the page one recurring object and re-pose it in every section (split, merged, crumpled, flattened, a vertical spike): one 3D or SVG glyph carries about ten screens of continuity without new imagery. Keep it clear of the reading text, which the site does not.
Change the ground colour through an edge that belongs to the theme (flame silhouettes, torn paper) instead of a straight cut, so the transition is itself a picture.

Scale a small card into a full-bleed band and scale its heading with it, so a statement arrives as an event instead of a fade. The site wedges a script word into its headlines; under the house rules a headline stays in one face and one colour.
media: On the fold the 3D emblem covers about 15% of the area as two halves on a black void; with the headline it takes about 60% of the centre. Pictures arrive as a centred flipping deck, a card that grows into a full-bleed band, and a vertical carousel over a blurred copy of itself: 29 images, three canvases, a full-viewport line diagram, no video.
motion: Lenis drives a scroll-scrubbed Three.js emblem that changes pose and scale per section across three pins of about 5440, 4560 and 4440px. Split words (297 elements) drift into lines on transform 2s cubic-bezier(0.075,0.82,0.165,1), skills type out character by character, panels move over .45s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1), and grain (0.09s steps), a 12s ring and a fluid field loop forever with no reduced-motion rule; load took about 6.6s.

name: Gionatan Nese
idea: A designer's portfolio shown as one object in an empty white room: about twenty small product-shot cards float as a slowly turning 3D sphere in the middle of a full-screen canvas, and the wheel turns the sphere instead of moving the page.
hero: A white loader first: three 16px items on the exact horizontal middle, the name in a grotesk at a 9vw left margin, a monogram assembling letter by letter in the centre, the job title in a serif ending at the same right margin, and a zero-padded serif percentage counter bottom-centre. Then a full-screen white WebGL canvas holds one sphere about 445px across centred at (720, 450): about twenty 3:4 portrait cards, 50-90px wide, each a product or object photograph on a flat light-grey or black plate. It fills 31% of the width and half the height, with white on every side. The only controls are a 216px group at top-centre (the monogram and three small view pills) and a 16px sound dot top-right. No headline: the largest type on the site is 16px.
type: Two families at one size. A neutral grotesk at weight 500 (78% of characters) for the name, monogram and project names; a delicate high-contrast serif at 400 (22%) for the job title, the view label and the counter. Everything is 14-16px (largest 1.1vw), sentence case, tracking 0. Hierarchy comes only from the change of face and from position.
colour: #ffffff #000000 #ececec #f0f0f0 — White ground on about 97% of the pixels, black text, light-grey or black card plates. The only colour is in the few saturated photographs inside the cards: a pink poster, a navy phone case, a dark red figure.
imagery: Photographs of the designer's products and objects, each plated on flat light grey (about three in four) or black, in one portrait ratio near 3:4, square corners, no border or shadow; depth is shown only by scale and overlap.
layout: No document sections: one fixed 1440x900 canvas, scrollY stays 0 and the wheel is captured. Everything aligns to the centre axis; the content takes the middle 31% of the width and the other 69% is white wall. On the phone the sphere widens to about 78% of the screen and the nav stays top-centre.

sections.description: The sphere is the only content. Each wheel step turns it, near cards grow and overlap the far ones, and it eases to a resting angle. Two other views of the same set sit behind the small pills; a list of project names at 16px on a 72px row pitch exists in the markup but was not visible in any capture.

steal: Unify mixed work by plating it: every project image on a flat light-grey or black plate in one portrait ratio with square corners, about three grey to one black, so twenty unrelated projects read as one catalogue.

Place one centred object at about 31% of the width and half the height and let the rest be wall; it reads as intentional only when nothing else competes. Under the house rules add a 16px caption under it with the front item's title and year, and a plain list view one click away.

Run the page at text size and let placement make the hierarchy only if the layout supplies the drama. The site has no title at all; the house version still puts the name and what the person does in a clear h1 on the first screen.
media: One full-screen WebGL canvas holds about twenty image textures as cards on a centred sphere; clearly non-white pixels add up to only 2-3% of the screen. No img or video elements and no drawings.
motion: A white loader assembles the monogram letter by letter while a serif counter ticks for over 5s, although the document loaded in 916ms. After that each wheel step turns the card sphere and eases it to rest, with no page scroll and no end; pills ease on cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) at 0.2-0.45s, and there are no keyframes, no split text and no reduced-motion rule.

name: Noomo Showcase
idea: An immersive studio's year in review opened like a launch sequence: while the page loads, one letter of the wordmark stretches into the progress bar, and then a single justified manifesto fills a starfield edge to edge, with a window in the shape of the brand glyph cut into its middle that glitches the words behind it.
hero: A fullscreen WebGL starfield. A five-line uppercase statement at about 90px (6.2vw), leading about 0.97, forced-justified from x=14 to about x=1410 and centred vertically (y 230-656), says this is the studio's year of 3D, motion and interactive web work; most words are in a light grotesk and four key phrases in a heavier cut that, in the opening state, sit on rounded electric-blue pills with bloom. At the exact centre a pixel-cross window about 360x420 displaces and thresholds the type behind it, with about twelve chrome spheres on its outline. A 57px header (logo, three small links, a sound toggle, an email button) and one small get-started button with a round arrow centred about 40px above the bottom. The headline lives in the canvas, not the DOM, and the wheel does nothing until the button is clicked.
type: PP Neue Montreal Book and Medium for names and the canvas headline (about 90px, uppercase, justified, light and heavy cuts mixed word by word); GT America Mono at 400 for 65% of the DOM characters (nav, buttons, tags) at 11-20px; a script flourish beside the logo. DOM sizes stay at 11, 14, 16 and 20px. The house version keeps the grotesk alone, puts the headline in the DOM in two lines, and drops the monospace.
colour: #000000 #d9e0ed #d2e0ff #0004eb #050516 — Black ground on about 75% of the screen, cool off-white text (82% of it), periwinkle for the loader wordmark and button chips. Electric blue is about 2% of the DOM but 15-25% of the screen in the opening state, as a glow band, phrase pills and the button, then drains to monochrome after a few seconds. The house version keeps the blue as a flat fill on the button and sets the key phrases plainly.
imagery: No photographs or video on the first screen: a starfield, a glitch window shaped like the brand glyph, and small glossy chrome spheres, all in one Three.js canvas. In the blue state, a bloom band, slight RGB fringing and scanline grit on the type; inside the cross the type is thresholded to harsh black-and-white noise.
layout: One fixed 1440x900 stage: a fullscreen canvas, a fixed smooth-scroll wrapper and a fixed overlay; scrollY stays 0 and the 17-screen document below was never reached. The statement runs edge to edge with about 14px gutters, with bands of starfield about 170px deep above and below, closed by the header and the button. Eight case studies wait in the DOM behind the click.

sections.description: The loader: a black screen with a wordmark of chunky pixel letters about 82px tall flush bottom-left in pale periwinkle and a 50px percentage counter above it. One round letter stretches sideways into a capsule as the count rises, so the logo is the progress bar: about 520px wide at 0%, 860px at 40% (where it stalls for over 2s) and 1300px at 91%.
Measured in the DOM but never visible: eight case-study entries with 20px names and tags and solid blue square-cornered buttons, reachable only after the hero button.

steal: Make one round letter of the wordmark a capsule that stretches, docked bottom-left at about 80px tall and growing from about 36% to 92% of the width. The site uses it as the progress of a loader; the house rules allow no preloader, so here it is the entrance: the page is readable on the first frame and the letter stretches once within 1.2s.

Let one statement be the whole hero, justified edge to edge with tight gutters and centred vertically with about 170px of ground above and below. The site runs it to five lines inside the canvas; under the house rules the headline is two lines, in the DOM, with a short paragraph under it for the rest.

Give the brand glyph a job: cut the logo's distinctive letterform as a window through a picture and treat what shows inside differently, so the mark reads as part of the content. The site cuts it through the headline, which the house rules forbid.
media: The canvas covers 100% of the first screen: the type plane takes about 97% of the width and 47% of the height, and the glitch cross with its spheres about 25% by 47% at the centre. One img (the header logo), one Three.js canvas, no video; any case-study pictures sit behind the click.
motion: The loader counts to 91% while one letter stretches into a capsule, stalling at 40% from 2.5s to at least 4.5s; the hero then opens in its electric-blue state and drains to monochrome on a timer, not on scroll, and the wheel does nothing until the button is clicked. The cross glitches the canvas type live, spans change filter over 0.4s and the header translates over 0.5s (both on cubic-bezier(0.65,0.05,0.36,1)), and a 2s bounce loop nudges the button arrow, with no reduced-motion rule.
